Roast potatoes for 15 minutes.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken with 3g garlic powder, 3g paprika, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Add chicken breasts to the baking sheet alongside the potatoes.
Add broccoli florets to the baking sheet. Drizzle broccoli with remaining 15ml olive oil. Toss gently.
Return baking sheet to oven. Continue roasting for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Breast with Savory Apple & Cherry Stuffing, Banana-Thyme Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken breast, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is plump, visibly stuffed beneath the skin with a savory mixture of pale diced apple and dark red chopped dried cherries. A rich, creamy, light tan banana-thyme pan sauce pools elegantly around the chicken. A fresh thyme sprig garnishes the dish. Composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Prepare stuffing: In a large pan, melt 15g butter and 5ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and celery. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add diced apple and chopped dried cherries. Cook 3 minutes. Stir in 3g fresh thyme.
Remove from heat. Transfer mixture to a bowl. Add breadcrumbs, 50ml milk, egg white, salt, and pepper. Mix well until combined. Do not overmix.
Prepare chicken: Gently loosen skin over chicken breasts to create a pocket. Carefully spoon stuffing mixture under skin, spreading evenly over breast meat. Do not overfill.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat 10ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts skin-side down 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken breasts. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at thickest part.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent with foil. Let rest 5-10 minutes.

Prepare banana-thyme pan sauce: While chicken rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add sliced banana, remaining 2g fresh thyme, and 10g sugar. Cook 2-3 minutes, mashing banana with a spoon.

Pour in chicken stock and remaining 50ml milk. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for a smoother consistency, if desired. Stir in remaining 15g butter until melted and incorporated.
Serve chicken: Place one roasted chicken breast on each plate. Spoon banana-thyme pan sauce generously around chicken. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.
Serve immediately, ensuring chicken is fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Garlic and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh sits on a simple off-white ceramic plate. The chicken is golden-brown on top, succulent beneath, partially submerged in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. Tender, roughly diced onion pieces and whole, soft garlic cloves are visible within the sauce, adding textural contrast. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley garnishes the dish. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A casual cloth napkin and everyday flatware are placed nearby. The scene conveys a homely, comforting family meal with natural, unforced presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add whole garlic cloves and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce, skin-side up.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C. Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve over pasta or polenta for a heartier meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Wild Mushroom Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Wild Mushroom Jus is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, seared beef medallion, golden-brown with a visible crust, is positioned centrally. Beside it, a quenelle of creamy, smooth potato puree gleams subtly. A rich, glossy wild mushroom jus, deep amber in color, is elegantly spooned over the beef and pooled around its base, showcasing various earthy brown mushroom pieces, some sliced, some quartered. A small sprig of fresh green thyme rests atop the beef medallion, adding a pop of vibrant color. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant-style setting with a casual atmosphere, focusing attention on the dish while suggesting a dining environment.
instructions: Peel and cube potatoes. Place in a pot with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
While potatoes cook, pat beef tenderloin medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil and 20g of butter in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef medallions in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. A dark, even crust should form.
Remove seared beef from the skillet and transfer to a warm plate. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for at least 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add another 20g of butter to the same skillet. Add finely diced shallots. Sauté until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced or quartered mixed wild mushrooms to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in the red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon. Let the wine reduce by half.
Add beef stock and fresh thyme sprigs to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook until the sauce has reduced and thickened slightly to a jus consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Remove thyme sprigs.

While the jus reduces, return drained potatoes to the hot pot. Mash thoroughly with the remaining 20g of butter and warm heavy cream or milk until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir chopped fresh parsley into the mushroom jus. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

To plate, place a generous scoop of creamy potato puree on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange one seared beef medallion next to the puree. Spoon the rich wild mushroom jus generously over and around the beef.
Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig or a sprinkle of extra chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Sautéed Apples and Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Skillet Chicken with Sautéed Apples and Linguine is presented on an everyday, round ceramic plate with a subtle off-white glaze. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 2.5 cm thick, are nestled among the pale-yellow linguine. Tender, thinly sliced apple pieces and soft, translucent diced onion are distributed throughout, adding subtle color variation. A light, savory glaze from the skillet coats the pasta and chicken, creating a comforting, cohesive look. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, providing a pop of color. The arrangement is casual and natural, as if served directly from the skillet onto the plate, with components touching and slightly overlapping. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a family kitchen environment. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a lived-in dining area, maintaining focus on the homely, expertly prepared comfort food.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add linguine. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Peel and thinly slice apples. Dice yellow onion. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced apples. Sauté 5-7 minutes until apples are tender-crisp.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried thyme. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly reduces.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet with the apple mixture. Stir to combine. Heat through.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet. Toss gently to coat pasta with sauce and combine all ingredients.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Kidney Bean Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Chicken and Kidney Bean Pilaf is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous single portion. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (approximately 3cm cubes) are nestled among fluffy, amber-hued long-grain rice. Diced carrots and onions (small cubes, 1cm) are interspersed, adding subtle color and texture. Plump kidney beans are evenly distributed throughout, providing a contrasting deep red. The dish is generously garnished with a vibrant scattering of freshly chopped green dill and parsley, enhancing its rustic appeal. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all bathed in soft, natural lighting, evoking a cozy bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers (ogurtsy).
Offer a dollop of sour cream (smetana) for individual serving.

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return chicken to the pot. Add drained and rinsed kidney beans and rice. Stir to combine.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during simmering.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped dill and parsley.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh dill and parsley.
notes: Ensure rice is fully cooked and fluffy.
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A deep, wide white porcelain bowl holds a generous individual portion of robust Pork Jambalaya. The dish presents a rich, inviting reddish-brown hue from the seasoned tomatoes and browned meats. Visible elements include tender, savory chunks of browned pork and slices of dark, caramelized Andouille sausage, interspersed with fluffy, distinct grains of long-grain rice. Bright green diced bell peppers, softened translucent onions, and celery pieces provide pops of color and texture contrast. The surface is lightly textured with a scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley. The composition is naturally flowing, not overly structured, reflecting a hearty, comforting meal. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and a sturdy, traditional-looking spoon, all bathed in soft, even natural light, creating an authentic bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot sauce on the side
Serve with cornbread
instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Brown pork on all sides until well-caramelized. Remove pork from pot.
Add sliced andouille sausage (if using) to the pot. Cook until browned. Remove sausage.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, green bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, dried thyme, and Cajun seasoning. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return browned pork and sausage to the pot. Stir in undrained diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Add rice. Stir once. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid or stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff jambalaya with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.
traditional_techniques: Using the 'Holy Trinity' (onion, celery, bell pepper) as a base

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Mustard Chicken and Mushroom Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente penne pasta forms a natural base, generously coated in a rich, velvety cream-mustard sauce. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 2-3 cm, showcasing tender interiors. Vibrant red and yellow bell pepper pieces, diced into uniform 1.5 cm squares, add pops of color and tender-crisp texture. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed until lightly browned, are nestled among the pasta and chicken. A delicate sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a few fresh oregano leaves provide a final touch. The dish maintains moderate negative space, appearing inviting and well-composed. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's warmth. Standard silver flatware rests beside the plate on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard European flatware on a white porcelain dinner plate.
instructions: Boil 4 litres of salted water in a large pot. Cook 400g penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 125ml pasta water.
Cut 600g chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add 1 diced medium onion and 3 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add 200g sliced cremini mushrooms and 2 diced bell peppers (red, yellow). Sauté 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften and mushrooms brown.
Stir in 200g diced tomatoes, 30g Dijon mustard, and 250ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Stir in 200ml heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Simmer 2 minutes until chicken is heated through and sauce thickens slightly.
Add drained pasta to the skillet. Toss well to coat with sauce. Add reserved pasta water if sauce is too thick.
Stir in 50g grated Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Roasted Poblano Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, free-flowing Chicken and Roasted Poblano Risotto is presented on a clean, wide white porcelain plate. The al dente Arborio rice forms a rich, off-white base, studded with golden-brown, tender diced chicken chunks. Vibrant green flecks of diced roasted poblano chili are visible throughout, along with subtle orange pieces of finely diced carrot, adding pops of color. The risotto has a luscious, fluid consistency, not dry or molded. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the center, with a light dusting of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's texture and sheen. A folded white cotton napkin and simple flatware are placed beside the plate, maintaining a clean, restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast poblano chilies for 15-20 minutes until skin blisters. Transfer to a bowl, cover, and cool. Peel, deseed, and dice the chilies. Set aside.
Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken and set aside.
Finely dice onion and carrot. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and 20g butter to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent. This toasts the rice.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in the cooked chicken chunks and diced roasted poblano chilies.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until risotto is creamy and emulsified. This is mantecatura.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Sage and Prosciutto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Saltimbocca is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The two golden-brown chicken pieces, seared to perfection, are positioned slightly overlapping, showcasing their crisp prosciutto and vibrant green sage leaves. A glossy, amber-hued pan sauce is generously spooned over and around the chicken, creating a glistening sheen. The chicken itself is plump, not sliced, retaining its natural form. A fresh lemon wedge and a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley add bright color and freshness. The plate is centered on a simple, rustic wooden table. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background. Traditional Italian flatware is placed beside the plate, completing the authentic bistro setting.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound chicken breasts to 6mm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper on both sides.
Lay two prosciutto slices flat on each chicken breast. Place 4-5 small sage leaves on top of the prosciutto.
Fold each chicken breast in half, enclosing the prosciutto and sage. Secure with a toothpick if needed.
Lightly dredge each chicken piece in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil and half of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add chicken to the skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm on a plate.
Add white wine to the hot skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer until sauce slightly thickens, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining butter and the juice of half a lemon until butter melts and sauce emulsifies.
Adjust seasoning if needed. Remove toothpicks from chicken.
Serve chicken immediately, spooning sauce generously over each piece.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thigh with Fermented Potato Gratin, Crispy Leek Greens, and Carrot Top Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and crisped, rests beside a generous, rectangular portion of golden-brown potato gratin on an earth-toned, handcrafted ceramic plate. The gratin shows distinct layers of thinly sliced potatoes, bubbling gently with a creamy texture. A vibrant green dollop of carrot top pesto is neatly placed adjacent to the chicken. Delicately crispy, golden-brown julienned leek greens are scattered artfully over the chicken and gratin, adding a textural contrast. The plate, in shades of cream and beige, is set on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery visible, emphasizing an eco-conscious, sustainable aesthetic. The composition is uncrowded, allowing ample negative space to highlight each component's beauty.

ingredients.name: Fermented Vegetable Brine (e.g., sauerkraut or kimchi brine)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
For the Potato Gratin: Peel potatoes. Slice into 2 mm thick rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife. Arrange half the slices in an oven-safe gratin dish.
In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, milk, minced garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Heat gently until just simmering. Stir in fermented vegetable brine.
Pour half the cream mixture over potatoes in the dish. Layer remaining potato slices. Pour remaining cream mixture over the top. Cover with foil.
Bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. Let rest.
For the Crispy Leek Greens: Wash dark green leek parts thoroughly. Slice into thin julienne strips. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry leek strips in batches until crispy and golden. Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

For the Carrot Top Pesto: Wash carrot tops thoroughly. Pat dry. In a food processor, combine carrot tops, toasted pumpkin seeds, remaining garlic clove, lemon juice, 60 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Process until smooth or desired consistency. Add more olive oil if needed.
For the Chicken Thighs: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.

To Serve: Place a generous portion of potato gratin on a handcrafted ceramic plate. Place a pan-seared chicken thigh next to the gratin. Spoon a dollop of carrot top pesto beside the chicken. Garnish with crispy leek greens on top of the chicken or gratin. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of creamy Cheesy Chicken Risotto is served in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, resting on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. The risotto is fluid and spreads naturally within the bowl, not mounded or shaped. Its color is a rich, creamy off-white with visible flecks of golden-brown seared chicken cubes (approximately 2 cm). The chicken pieces are tender, some peeking through the rice, showcasing their slightly browned exterior. The texture is soft and yielding, characteristic of properly cooked risotto. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley adorns the top, providing a subtle color contrast. A simple, silver spoon rests casually beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, creating soft shadows. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining olive oil and 30 g butter to the pot.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add 240 ml of warm chicken stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Continue adding stock, 240 ml at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Fold in cooked chicken. Stir well.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: For extra richness, a splash of cream can be added at the end with the butter and cheese.
Any leftover risotto can be formed into arancini and fried the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden pappardelle pasta, gently tossed in a creamy, blush-toned sauce, forms the base. Thick medallions of seared chicken thigh are arranged naturally atop the pasta, showcasing their golden-brown crust. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding color and freshness. Julienne strips of rich red sun-dried tomatoes provide visual depth. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded linen napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a subtly blurred background hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere. The composition is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, julienned
Dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest. Do not clean the skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-5 minutes until they begin to soften and burst.
Pour in white wine or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Return to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Slice rested chicken thighs into thick medallions.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce in the skillet. Cook until just wilted.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and lemon juice. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in sliced chicken medallions.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken in Roasted Chili Sauce with Corn and Butternut Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender chicken chunks, bathed in a rich, dark red roasted ancho and guajillo chili sauce, is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is seared and then simmered, retaining its rustic, whole chunk form. Beside the chicken, vibrant orange cubes of roasted butternut squash, slightly caramelized, are thoughtfully arranged with bright yellow, sautéed corn kernels. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped green cilantro and a few bright green, thinly sliced pickled jalapeños, adding a pop of color and acidity. The textures are varied: succulent chicken, smooth sauce, tender squash, and crisp-tender corn. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin, and a stack of warm corn tortillas placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Serve with Mexican rice
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from dried chilies. Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let soak for 20 minutes until soft.
Peel and dice butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast squash at 200°C (390°F) for 20-25 minutes. Squash should be tender and slightly caramelized.

Drain rehydrated chilies. Blend chilies with Roma tomatoes, 1/2 chopped white onion, garlic, 250ml chicken broth, cumin, and Mexican oregano until smooth. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for a smoother consistency. Discard solids.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Pour strained chili sauce into the pot. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken to the pot. Add remaining 250ml chicken broth.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and sauce should thicken slightly.
While chicken simmers, sauté corn kernels in a small pan with a touch of oil until tender-crisp. Season lightly.
Portion chicken and sauce onto individual plates. Arrange roasted butternut squash and sautéed corn beside the chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and sliced pickled jalapeños. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Toasting and rehydrating dried chilies for sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons is nested in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. A whole, bone-in braised chicken thigh rests centrally on the pasta, showing a rich, caramelized exterior. Small, tender cubes of carrot and celery, along with dark, wrinkled Kalamata olives, are distributed throughout the sauce. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid green garnish. The dish is set on a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Chianti wine
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in wine. Deglaze the pan bottom.
Add tomatoes and olives. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover.
Simmer 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with sauce.
Place pasta in bowls. Top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the wide pasta ribbons
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Creamy Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of golden-hued tagliatelle is artfully swirled onto a clean white porcelain dinner plate, forming a comforting nest. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy sauce, subtly infused with earthy tones from pan-seared, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms and vibrant green, wilted spinach. Scattered amongst the pasta are succulent, irregularly shaped chunks of pan-seared chicken breast, each piece boasting a beautiful golden-brown crust. The dish is garnished with a light sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley and delicate shavings of aged Parmesan cheese, adding freshness and a touch of elegance. The presentation on a simple wooden table, alongside a standard set of flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evokes a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Freshly grated Parmesan cheese
Crusty bread for dipping sauce
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add diced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60 ml of pasta water.
Add spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and seared chicken chunks to the sauce. Add grated Parmesan cheese. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Sausage and Bell Pepper Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: The Smoked Sausage and Bell Pepper Rice Skillet is presented as a generous individual portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Golden-brown smoked sausage rounds are interspersed with earthy brown rice and kidney beans. Bright red and green diced bell peppers add freshness, complemented by yellow corn kernels. A rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce, infused with achiote, coats all ingredients, providing a cohesive look. The ingredients are piled naturally in the center of the plate, creating a balanced and inviting mound. The surface is lightly scattered with fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a minimal, blurred restaurant background. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space surrounding the food.

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Slice smoked sausage into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausage rounds to skillet. Cook until browned on both sides. Remove sausage and set aside.
Dice onion into small pieces. Dice bell peppers into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion and bell peppers to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, achiote paste, oregano, and basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Stir in rinsed kidney beans and corn kernels.
Pour in vegetable broth. Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in cooked brown rice. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken with Peppers and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, rustic ceramic plate holds a generous, homely portion of Spanish-Style Chicken with Peppers and Tomatoes. One bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and crisped, sits nestled in a rich, vibrant red-orange sauce. Thick, softened strips of red and green bell peppers and tender chunks of tomato are visible around and under the chicken, contributing natural, earthy colors. The sauce is thick and rustic, clinging to the ingredients. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final, simple garnish. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A crinkled, plain linen napkin and a piece of crusty bread are casually placed beside it. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful sauce.
Serve alongside simple white rice.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add sliced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce and vegetables. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes if sauce needs to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs adds more flavor and keeps the chicken moist.
This dish reheats well, making it great for leftovers.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Spicy Italian Sausage and Broccolini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of orecchiette pasta coated in a light, emulsified sauce. The pasta is interspersed with browned, crumbled Italian sausage chunks, providing a rustic texture and savory color. Bright green, tender-crisp broccolini pieces are distributed throughout, adding vibrant color and a fresh counterpoint. Thinly sliced garlic slivers and flecks of red chili flakes are visible, hinting at the aromatic and spicy notes. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese covers the top, with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley providing a final flourish. The plating is organized but natural, allowing elements to mix freely. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface with a neutral cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano at the table.
Pair with a light-bodied red wine like Chianti or a crisp white wine.

ingredients.name: Broccolini
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, trimmed, cut into 3 cm pieces

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage meat. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Drain excess fat from the pan, if any. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes to the pan with the sausage. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add broccolini to the pan. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Pour in white wine to deglaze the pan. Scrape up any browned bits.
Add drained pasta to the pan with the sausage and broccolini. Pour in 120 ml of reserved pasta water. Toss well to combine.
Stir in grated Pecorino Romano cheese. Add more pasta water, 30 ml at a time, if needed to create a light sauce that coats the pasta. The sauce should be fluid, not dry.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Pecorino Romano.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.
Ensure pasta is truly al dente for best texture.
The pasta water is crucial for creating the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening from its pan juices, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole, succulent piece. Surrounding the chicken are vibrantly colored roasted vegetables: large chunks of caramelized red and yellow bell peppers, tender thick half-moons of zucchini with slight charring, softened red onion wedges, and burst cherry tomatoes. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are interspersed amongst the vegetables, adding deep green accents. A light, savory pan sauce from the roasting process lightly coats the chicken and vegetables. The plate features balanced negative space, ensuring the dish is the focal point. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside the plate, illuminated by natural, even lighting for an inviting, casual bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut red and yellow bell peppers into large 3cm chunks. Cut zucchini into thick 2cm half-moons. Cut red onion into 2cm wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes.
In a large oven-safe skillet or roasting pan, heat 30ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first if skin-on, for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.

Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add bell peppers, zucchini, red onion, and cherry tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften and caramelize.
Stir in minced garlic, fresh rosemary, fresh thyme, and chopped oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with chicken broth and white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them among the vegetables. Squeeze juice from one lemon half over the chicken and vegetables. Place the squeezed lemon half in the pan.
Transfer the skillet or roasting pan to the preheated oven.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes in the pan.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Meat and Potato Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Meat and Potato Macaroni Bake is presented in a deep, round ceramic bowl with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. The top layer of the bake is a golden-brown, slightly uneven crust of mashed potato and macaroni, showing visible melted cheddar cheese and crisp, toasted breadcrumbs. A spoonful has been taken, revealing the rich, dark brown meat and vegetable filling underneath. The filling is hearty, with discernible chunks of orange diced carrots, red diced bell pepper, bright green peas, and yellow corn kernels. A few vibrant green chopped fresh basil leaves are scattered over the exposed filling and the potato crust. A small cluster of fresh, delicate green sunflower sprouts sits casually on the side of the bowl. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm, soft lighting from an overhead fixture, casting gentle shadows. A simple, off-white ceramic plate with a fork rests beside the bowl. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin completes the homely scene. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a modest, satisfying portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish at the family table.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef and ground chicken. Cook until browned, breaking up meat with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, diced carrots, and diced bell pepper to the pot. Cook until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, Dijon mustard, dried thyme, dried savory, dried marjoram, paprika, and ground grains of paradise. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in dark beer, pork stock, Worcestershire sauce, and verjus. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
While meat simmers, boil potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Mash potatoes with milk, butter, and half of the grated cheddar cheese until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Add frozen green peas and corn to the simmering meat mixture. Stir well.
Stir cooked macaroni into the mashed potato mixture.
Spoon the meat and vegetable filling into the bottom of an oven-safe baking dish.
Spread the potato-macaroni topping evenly over the meat filling.
Sprinkle remaining grated cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs over the topping.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with chopped fresh basil and sunflower sprouts.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Grains of paradise can be substituted with freshly ground black pepper for a milder flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peruvian Arroz con Pollo is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing vibrant colors and textures. Two golden-brown, seared chicken pieces, a thigh and a drumstick, are prominently nestled atop a generous bed of fluffy, emerald-green rice. The rice is infused with cilantro, speckled with bright red diced bell pepper and tender green peas, and small diced carrots. The chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the dish as a garnish, adding a burst of fresh green. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich hues and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Salsa Criolla (sliced red onion, aji limo, lime juice, and cilantro).
Pair with a glass of Chicha Morada or Inca Kola.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do this in batches to avoid crowding the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced red onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in aji amarillo paste, cumin powder, and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
In a blender, combine fresh cilantro with 100 ml of chicken broth. Blend until smooth to create a vibrant green cilantro paste.
Add rice to the pot with the cooked aromatics. Stir to coat the rice, toasting for 2 minutes.
Pour in the dark beer (or chicken broth) and remaining chicken broth. Stir in the cilantro paste. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in frozen green peas and small diced carrots. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving. Check chicken internal temperature, it should be 75°C (167°F).
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Ziti with Sausage and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual serving of baked ziti with sausage and ricotta is presented on a simple, rustic ceramic plate with a slightly chipped rim. The pasta, baked to a golden-brown crust on top, shows rich, melted mozzarella and golden-brown Parmesan cheese bubbling over a hearty red tomato sauce. Chunks of browned Italian sausage are visible throughout the pasta and sauce. The pasta itself is tender, coated in the creamy ricotta and tomato mixture. A few vibrant green basil leaves are scattered loosely on top. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, perhaps with a slight scratch or two. A plain linen or cotton napkin, perhaps folded simply or casually tossed, is beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a kitchen in the late afternoon. No fancy garnishes or precise arrangements, just comforting food ready to be enjoyed.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread
Simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta al dente according to package directions. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Remove sausage casings. Add sausage meat to pot. Break apart with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer 15 minutes.
Season sauce with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped fresh basil.
In a large bowl, combine cooked pasta, half the tomato sauce, ricotta cheese, half the shredded mozzarella, and half the grated Parmesan. Mix well.
Spoon half the pasta mixture into a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Top with remaining tomato sauce.
Sprinkle remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Herb Salad with Chicken and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, featuring a vibrant, balanced composition. A bed of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens forms the base. Piled artfully on top are roasted potato cubes, their skins slightly browned, revealing a tender interior. Interspersed are soft, caramelized red onion wedges and small, evenly diced pieces of roasted chicken, golden-brown and juicy. A creamy, pale yellow garlic-Parmesan dressing lightly coats the potato and chicken mixture, showing its rich texture. Sprinkled throughout are vibrant green flecks of fresh parsley and chives, adding color and freshness. Shaved Parmesan curls are scattered generously over the top, catching the light. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a relaxed bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Cut red onion into 2cm wedges. Peel 4 garlic cloves.
Toss potatoes, onion, and whole garlic cloves with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breast dry. Rub with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breast 3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer skillet to oven. Roast chicken for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice chicken into 1.5cm cubes.
For the dressing: In a bowl, whisk mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, minced garlic, grated parmesan, salt, and pepper. Add water gradually to reach desired pourable consistency.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, roasted onion, and diced chicken. Add beef stock to the warm roasted vegetables and chicken, tossing gently to coat.
Add chopped parsley, chopped chives, and half of the shaved parmesan to the potato mixture. Pour dressing over the mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Arrange mixed salad greens on serving plates. Spoon potato and chicken mixture over the greens.
Garnish with remaining shaved parmesan. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Tomato Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Beef and Tomato Rice Skillet rests in an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl. Thick chunks of tender, slow-cooked beef are nestled among fluffy, tomato-stained rice and soft, diced onions. Vibrant red diced tomatoes and hints of minced garlic are visible throughout the rich, savory mixture. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The dish has a natural, comforting appearance, as if just served from the stove. It sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a lived-in, family kitchen atmosphere. A simple metal fork and a casually placed cloth napkin complete the homely setting. The portion is modest and inviting, showcasing a truly comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add beef chunks. Brown beef on all sides. Remove beef from skillet.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to skillet. Stir in diced tomatoes, beef broth, rice, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Cover skillet.
Reduce heat to low. Cook 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir well. Remove from heat. Let rest 5 minutes, covered.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey and Spinach Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely scoop of Turkey and Spinach Pasta Bake fills a simple round ceramic plate, just served from a rustic baking dish. The short pasta is thoroughly coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce, revealing visible crumbles of browned ground turkey and tender, dark green wilted spinach leaves. The top surface of the bake features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted Parmesan cheese, with caramelized, slightly crispy edges. The dish offers natural colors: deep reds, vibrant greens, and warm golden-browns. Textures are a comforting blend of tender pasta, succulent turkey, and gooey cheese. The plating is casual, a true home-style serving. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, bathed in warm, natural kitchen light. A plain cloth napkin and standard flatware complete the simple, inviting scene, emphasizing its comfort food appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cook pasta al dente according to package directions. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add ground turkey. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth (if using). Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in fresh spinach until completely wilted into the sauce.
Add cooked pasta to the turkey sauce in the pan. Mix well to combine.
Sprinkle half of the grated Parmesan cheese over the pasta mixture. Gently stir to distribute.
Top the pasta mixture with the remaining grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Orecchiette, Burst Tomato, and Cucumber-Feta Garnish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Orecchiette, Burst Tomato, and Cucumber-Feta Garnish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The orecchiette pasta, coated in a light, vibrant red sauce from the burst cherry tomatoes, forms the base. Some cherry tomatoes remain whole, others are gently burst, releasing their juices into the sauce. Golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is nestled among the pasta. A generous scattering of crisp, small-diced green cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, and crumbled white feta cheese adds contrasting colors and textures over the dish. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed as a final garnish. The composition is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting colors. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere, subtly out of focus to keep the dish as the primary focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine or sparkling water with lemon.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions or large chunks.
Cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and burst.
Pour in chicken broth and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer. Stir in chopped fresh oregano.
Add drained orecchiette to the pan with the tomato sauce. Toss to coat. Cook 1-2 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Finely dice cucumber into small cubes. Thinly slice the red onion.
Stir half of the fresh basil into the pasta. Zest half the lemon into the pasta. Add a squeeze of lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Divide pasta among 4 plates. Arrange sliced chicken medallions or chunks over the pasta.
Garnish each plate with diced cucumber, thin red onion slices, crumbled feta cheese, and remaining fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust amount of lemon juice to personal preference for brightness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused golden bomba rice forms a slightly mounded base, interspersed with vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and bright green peas. Substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled atop and within the rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The plating is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Cook until wine is almost evaporated.
Stir in the bomba rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Add chicken broth and saffron (steeped in 30 ml warm broth). Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Check seasoning and adjust.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use good quality smoked paprika and authentic saffron threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Italian Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Baked Penne with Italian Sausage rests in a warm-toned, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The penne pasta, coated in a rich, red marinara sauce, is intertwined with crumbled, browned Italian sausage. Melted, golden-brown mozzarella cheese forms a bubbly, slightly uneven crust over the top, with pockets of creamy white ricotta peeking through. A scattering of fresh, torn green basil leaves adds a pop of natural color and freshness. The dish appears hearty and comforting, with natural, slightly uneven layers. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad

ingredients.name: Italian sausage (mild or hot), casings removed

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook penne pasta in salted water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage. Break apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in marinara sauce. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine cooked penne and sausage-marinara sauce. Mix well.
Spread half of the pasta mixture into a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Dollop half of the ricotta cheese over the pasta. Sprinkle with half of the mozzarella.
Add remaining pasta mixture. Dollop remaining ricotta. Top with remaining mozzarella and grated Parmesan.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil.
notes: For a spicier dish, use hot Italian sausage.
Bell peppers can be added with the onions for extra flavor and vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A deep, white porcelain bowl holds a generous individual portion of Pork Ragu with Pappardelle. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown ragu. Tender, shredded pork chunks are visible throughout the sauce, integrated seamlessly. Finely diced vegetables like onion, carrot, and celery have cooked down into the thick, flavorful sauce. A few small, vibrant red chili slices peek through, hinting at a gentle warmth. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped bright green flat-leaf parsley and a generous dusting of finely grated white Pecorino Romano cheese. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, along with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting its inviting textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a clean, casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until well-browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced deseeded red chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaves, and rosemary sprig. Stir to combine.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours. Cook until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves and rosemary stem from the pot. Use two forks to shred the pork directly in the sauce. Mix well.
Cook pappardelle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve hot. Garnish with freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley and grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
notes: The ragu can be made a day in advance; its flavor often improves overnight.
Adjust the amount of red chilies based on desired spice level. For less heat, remove all seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean braised chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thigh is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are tender, quartered new potatoes and vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes, all coated in a rich, rustic tomato-infused sauce. Sliced red bell peppers and dark Kalamata olives are interspersed, adding color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and a fork and knife beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its savory appeal with a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy. This takes 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear for 2 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add sliced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken broth, cherry tomatoes, quartered potatoes, oregano, and thyme sprigs to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them among the vegetables and liquid.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and braise for 30 minutes.
Remove lid. Continue to braise for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. The sauce will thicken slightly.
Stir in pitted Kalamata olives during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Discard thyme sprigs.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty chicken and potato soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The golden-amber broth fills the bowl, with generous, irregular chunks of tender chicken visible alongside soft, diced potatoes, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and light green celery pieces. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley rests on the soup's surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are comforting and wholesome, reflecting the home-cooked nature of the dish. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with natural imperfections. A simple, worn spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. The scene is lit by warm, cozy light from kitchen fixtures, creating a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere with natural, unobtrusive clutter in the background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Dice carrots into 1 cm rounds. Dice celery into 1 cm pieces. Chop onion.
Add onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince garlic. Add garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced potatoes, carrots, celery, and bay leaf. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred chicken into bite-sized pieces using two forks. Discard bay leaf.
Return shredded chicken to the soup. Stir well.
Season soup with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spaghetti Carbonara is artfully twirled into a neat mound on a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta, glistening with a rich, creamy, golden-yellow emulsion, forms the central focus. Scattered generously over the spaghetti are crispy, golden-brown cubes of rendered guanciale, adding textural contrast and deep savory notes. A generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese blankets parts of the dish, creating a delicate white layer. Freshly cracked black pepper provides dark speckles across the creamy surface. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a classic silver fork and spoon placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the pasta's sheen and the guanciale's crisp edges. The overall presentation is refined yet inviting, embodying a modern bistro style with authentic Italian simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine or sparkling water.
Traditionally eaten with a fork, using a spoon to assist in twirling the pasta.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Dice guanciale into 1 cm cubes.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced guanciale. Cook slowly until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy guanciale. Leave rendered fat in pan.
Cook spaghetti in boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, whisk egg yolks, whole egg, and 80 g grated Pecorino Romano in a bowl. Add half of the freshly ground black pepper.
Drain spaghetti. Add hot spaghetti directly to the pan with rendered guanciale fat. Toss to coat.
Immediately add egg mixture to spaghetti. Stir quickly and vigorously.
Gradually add reserved hot pasta water, 30 ml at a time, while stirring constantly. Continue until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms.
Add crispy guanciale back to the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining grated Pecorino Romano and fresh black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spanish Braised Chicken with Potatoes is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl. A succulent, bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, deeply caramelized and braised to tenderness, rests as the centerpiece, glistening with a rich, reddish-brown sauce. Surrounding the chicken are substantial 2-3 cm chunks of fork-tender potatoes, infused with the savory tomato-based sauce. Softened diced onions and small, tender pieces of cooked tomato are scattered throughout, adding textural contrast. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a bright green counterpoint. The sauce is medium-thick, clinging beautifully to all ingredients, with a subtle sheen from olive oil. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white porcelain dinner plate underneath the bowl, and a rustic linen napkin placed beside. A small terracotta ramekin with crusty bread and a glass of red wine are subtly in the background, enhancing the authentic Spanish bistro feel. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's comforting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a robust Spanish red wine.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and bay leaf. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Add potatoes cut into 2-3 cm chunks around the chicken.
Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pan.
Simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Penne with Fresh Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken and Penne with Fresh Tomato-Basil Sauce is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate, resting on a simple light wooden table. The al dente penne pasta, coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce with visible halved cherry tomatoes and flecks of green basil, forms the base. Three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, showing a slight char, are nestled among the pasta. The dish is garnished generously with fresh, bright green basil leaves and a dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese. A subtle drizzle of olive oil adds a touch of sheen. The composition is balanced, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. A silver fork and knife are placed to the side, and a folded cotton napkin completes the simple, inviting bistro setting under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a light-bodied red wine like Chianti or a crisp white wine.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 8-10 minutes, pressing gently to burst some tomatoes, until sauce thickens.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
