recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coq au Vin is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, coated in a glossy, deep-burgundy wine sauce. Surrounding the chicken are whole, golden-brown button mushrooms, translucent pearl onions, and crispy bacon lardons. The sauce is rich and thick, clinging to the meat. A pinch of fresh green parsley is scattered over the top. The background features a dark wood bistro table with a clean white cotton napkin and a small side plate of crusty baguette. Natural, even lighting highlights the velvety texture of the sauce and the rustic, braised appearance of the vegetables. The entire plate is visible with elegant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of the same red wine used in the braise
Serve in wide, shallow bowls

ingredients.name: dry red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until skin is golden. Remove from pot.
Fry bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp.
Add whole pearl onions and whole mushrooms to the bacon fat. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in red wine and chicken stock.
Add thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Mix butter and flour into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste into the simmering liquid to thicken the sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until glossy. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry red wine for the best flavor profile
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Relish and Aromatic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, placed on a light reclaimed wood surface. A golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, unsliced, rests on one side. Adjacent, a neat mound of fluffy, aromatic rice, subtly tinted by tomato, sits. A vibrant, chunky lacto-fermented tomato relish, showcasing bright red and orange hues, is spooned beside the chicken. A verdant drizzle of garlic green oil artfully zigzags over the rice. The plate is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. A small sprig of fresh parsley provides a natural, subtle garnish. The setting features an undyed linen napkin and soft, diffused natural lighting, creating an eco-conscious, minimalist aesthetic that highlights the ingredients' pure beauty.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Relish: Roughly chop 500g tomatoes. Mince 2 garlic cloves. In a bowl, combine chopped tomatoes, minced garlic, and 10g fine sea salt. Mash gently to release juices. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely or with an airlock. Let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours until slightly bubbly and tangy. Stir once or twice. (Can be used fresh if time is short, but tanginess will be less pronounced.)
Prepare Garlic Green Oil: Roughly chop garlic scapes or parsley. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Blend scapes/parsley, minced garlic, and 60ml olive oil until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Cook Aromatic Rice: Rinse 300g rice until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, heat a drizzle of olive oil. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Add minced garlic and 15g tomato paste. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add rinsed rice. Stir to coat. Pour in 500ml vegetable stock or water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 12-15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Score chicken skin lightly. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden-brown. Flip chicken. Continue cooking 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

Plate Dish: Place a portion of aromatic rice on each plate. Arrange a seared chicken thigh next to the rice. Spoon a generous amount of fermented tomato relish beside the chicken. Drizzle garlic green oil over the rice. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing full ingredients. Chicken trimmings and bones can be used for stock. Tomato ends and cores can be incorporated into the relish or stock.
The fermentation of the tomato relish adds a complex, tangy flavor and aids in food preservation.
Adjust the fermentation time for the relish based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Crispy Potato Rosti
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork tenderloin with crispy potato rosti is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A round, golden-brown potato rosti, approximately 10 cm in diameter, sits centrally. Beside it, two to three thick-cut, rosy pink pork medallions, each about 2 cm thick, are artfully arranged, showcasing their tender, juicy interior and beautifully seared exterior. A rich, glossy, deep amber apple cider reduction is generously drizzled around the plate and over the pork. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish, adding a touch of color. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting for a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel and coarsely grate potatoes. Place grated potatoes in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer dried grated potatoes to a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Heat 30g butter and 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Form potato mixture into four equal round patties, approximately 2 cm thick. Place patties in hot pan.
Cook rosti for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
While rosti bakes, pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork tenderloin on all sides until deeply browned, about 8-10 minutes total.
Transfer pork tenderloin to a baking sheet. Roast in the oven for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove from oven, rest for 5 minutes.
For the apple cider reduction, return the pan used for searing pork to medium heat. Add diced shallots, cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Deglaze pan with apple cider, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken stock and two thyme sprigs.

Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half until it coats the back of a spoon, about 8-10 minutes. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Stir in remaining 30g butter until melted and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested pork tenderloin into thick medallions, approximately 2 cm thick. Do not fan slices.
Plate one crispy potato rosti per person. Arrange pork medallions beside or slightly stacked on top of the rosti. Drizzle generously with warm apple cider reduction. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Spiced Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Indian Spiced Chicken Curry is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rich, reddish-brown curry, thick and glossy, features generous 3-4 cm chunks of tender chicken visible within the sauce. The surface is speckled with vibrant green chopped fresh coriander leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The curry's texture is smooth and inviting. Beside the bowl, a small, perfectly mounded portion of fluffy white basmati rice sits on a matching white porcelain dinner plate. A piece of warm, golden-brown naan bread is neatly folded and placed beside the rice. A small, simple ceramic bowl of white raita is positioned nearby. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a natural cotton napkin positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet approachable aesthetic, honoring its cultural origins.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm basmati rice.
Accompany with fresh naan bread or roti.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or a simple kachumber salad.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Set aside.
Heat oil or ghee in a large pot or karahi over medium-high heat.
Add cumin seeds. Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds (this is tempering, or 'tadka').
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in garlic paste and ginger paste. Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Reduce heat to medium. Add ground coriander, ground cumin, ground fennel, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Stir well for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if mixture sticks.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until the oil separates from the mixture.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Stir to coat chicken evenly with the spice mixture.
Pour in water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in salt to taste and garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes uncovered.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves.
Separately, cook basmati rice according to package instructions.
notes: Adjust red chili powder to preferred spice level.
For a richer curry, a spoon of yogurt or cream can be stirred in at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Mushrooms, Tomatoes, and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned braised chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its skin is a deep, burnished golden-brown. Surrounding the chicken is a rustic medley of braised vegetables: chunky, tender 2-3cm potato pieces, halved meaty button mushrooms, and vibrant diced tomatoes. All elements are coated in a rich, glossy, dark amber braising sauce, which pools invitingly at the base of the plate. The textures are soft and yielding. A generous sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped bright green parsley provides a vibrant contrast and freshness. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard European flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, soft lighting, presenting an inviting and wholesome casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Red wine, such as a Pinot Noir or Cabernet Franc.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pot. Add diced onions. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add flour. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in tomato paste. Add chicken broth, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add halved or quartered potatoes, mushrooms, and diced tomatoes around the chicken. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs.
The sauce will thicken naturally from the flour and reduction.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Carne
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Arroz con Pollo y Carne is presented in a clean, wide white porcelain bowl. The medium-grain rice forms the base, vibrant golden from saffron, cooked to a fluid, moist consistency with individual grains visible. Nestled within the rice are tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (5cm) and rich, braised beef cubes (4cm). Interspersed are soft, pale yellow potato cubes (2cm) and vibrant pieces of diced red and green bell pepper (1.5cm). The dish features a harmonious blend of colors: the deep golden rice, warm brown meats, bright red and green vegetables. Textures include fluffy rice, tender chicken, melting beef, and soft potatoes. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, light-colored wooden table surface holds the bowl. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate, alongside standard silver flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's textures. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side.
Provide hot sauce or Aji Amarillo for individual preference.
instructions: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Sear beef until well browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the pan. Sauté for 8 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika, cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in 250ml hot broth to deglaze the pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken and beef to the pan. Add potato cubes. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add rice to the pan. Pour in the remaining 950ml hot broth and the saffron steeped in warm broth. Stir gently to combine. Ensure liquid covers rice and ingredients.
Increase heat to medium-high. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice absorbs most liquid and is tender. Do not stir excessively during this stage.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Discard bay leaf. Check internal temperature of chicken, ensure it reaches 75°C.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Beef Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Chicken and Beef Vegetable Bake is presented in a modest, round ceramic bowl, resting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features a hearty base of browned ground beef and tender shredded chicken, generously mixed with vibrant diced tomatoes, dark sliced black olives, and earthy chopped Swiss chard. Bright green broccoli florets are arranged on top, partially submerged in the meaty base. A golden-brown, bubbly layer of melted American cheese blankets the entire dish, showing slight charring at the edges. A simple checkered cloth napkin lies casually beside the bowl, and a fork rests nearby. Warm, soft lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Poach chicken breasts in simmering water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove, cool slightly, then shred. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet with the beef. Cook until onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes, chopped Swiss chard (stems removed), and sliced black olives to the beef mixture. Cook for 5-7 minutes until chard wilts.
Stir in shredded chicken, salt, and black pepper. Mix well. Transfer this mixture to the prepared baking dish.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well. Arrange broccoli evenly over the chicken and beef mixture in the baking dish.
Lay American cheese slices over the broccoli, covering the entire top surface.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden brown. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Arroz
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pollo con Arroz is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its skin visibly crisp, is nestled into a vibrant, fluffy bed of tomato-infused rice. The long-grain rice is a rich orange-red hue, speckled with bright yellow corn kernels, finely diced green bell pepper, and fresh green cilantro. A few fresh cilantro sprigs are artfully scattered over the top. Two lime wedges are placed beside the chicken. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side, and a small stack of warm corn tortillas in a traditional basket, creating an authentic Mexican casual dining scene. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimal, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer fresh salsa or pico de gallo on the side.
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing over the dish.
Accompany with pickled jalapeños or a simple cabbage slaw.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, dried oregano, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, corn kernels, and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Carefully nestle seared chicken thighs back into the rice mixture, skin-side up.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in half of the chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately with remaining fresh cilantro and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom and Bacon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy sauce, highlighting browned mushrooms and crispy bacon lardons. Al dente tagliatelle pasta is neatly arranged beside the chicken. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with crispy exteriors, are artfully placed. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, small cubes of fresh mozzarella, and bright green chopped coriander garnish the dish, adding pops of color and freshness. Textures showcase crisp chicken skin, velvety sauce, tender pasta, and fluffy potatoes. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with standard cutlery and a cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, presenting a professional yet inviting appearance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes until golden and tender. Turn once during cooking.

While potatoes roast, cut bacon into 1 cm lardons. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bacon lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve bacon fat in the skillet.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Add 15ml olive oil to the skillet with bacon fat. Increase heat to high. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.

Reduce skillet heat to medium. Slice mushrooms thinly. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Add onion and mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour chicken stock into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Add double cream. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Stir in the cooked crispy bacon. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Add butter. Stir until melted.
While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Toss lightly with a drizzle of olive oil.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop fresh coriander. Cut mozzarella into small cubes or tear into pieces.

To serve, place a portion of pasta on each plate. Top with one pan-seared chicken breast. Spoon generous amounts of creamy mushroom and bacon sauce over the chicken and pasta. Arrange roasted potato wedges beside the chicken. Garnish with halved cherry tomatoes, fresh mozzarella pieces, and chopped coriander.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for thicker or adding a splash of stock for thinner.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Ragu with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rich, slow-braised beef ragu is elegantly plated atop a nest of wide, flat pappardelle pasta on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The ragu, a deep reddish-brown, features tender, chunky pieces of beef, visibly shredded from slow cooking, nestled within the thick, savory tomato sauce. Scattered around the pasta and ragu are golden-orange, roasted butternut squash chunks, their edges slightly caramelized. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped Italian parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork, reflecting natural, even lighting. The overall composition is professional, inviting, and balanced, showcasing the hearty textures and rich colors of the Italian classic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Accompany with a glass of robust Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and deseed butternut squash. Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Set aside.

Pat beef chuck dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 20ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring occasionally. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen flavor.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-4 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaf, and rosemary sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally. Remove bay leaf and rosemary sprig. Shred beef slightly with a fork within the sauce.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain.
Combine cooked pasta with the beef ragu. Toss to coat well. Stir in roasted butternut squash cubes.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with freshly chopped parsley and grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Creamy Dijon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef, cut into thick, irregular chunks, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef boasts a deep golden-brown crust and a tender, pink interior. A generous pool of creamy, pale-yellow Dijon sauce coats the beef, glistening subtly. Alongside, golden-crisp roasted potato wedges are arranged naturally, their fluffy interiors peeking out. Vibrant blanched green beans provide a fresh color contrast. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into thick wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast 30-35 minutes until golden and crisp.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water 3 minutes. Drain and shock in ice water. Drain well.
Pat beef steaks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat a large cast-iron or heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat. Add 15ml olive oil.
Sear steaks 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Ensure internal temperature reaches 63°C for medium-rare.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Rest 5-10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced shallots to the same pan. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Deglaze pan with cognac (if using), scraping up browned bits. Cook 1 minute.
Add beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Whisk until smooth. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in 30g butter until melted and incorporated. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Reheat green beans briefly in the pan with a knob of butter or steam.
Slice rested beef into thick chunks.
Plate individual portions: arrange roasted potato wedges, green beans, and beef chunks. Spoon generous amount of creamy Dijon sauce over beef. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Peperoni e Pomodori
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Risotto ai Peperoni e Pomodori is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto is a rich, creamy orange-red hue, indicating the incorporation of finely diced tomatoes and bell peppers. Its texture appears fluid and glossy, not dry, with visible small, tender chunks of red and yellow bell pepper and tomato. The al dente rice grains are distinct yet enveloped in a luscious, unctuous sauce. A small, artful cluster of fresh green basil leaves is placed off-center as a garnish, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. The bowl rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon. A folded white cotton napkin lies beside the bowl. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual Italian bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto quality diminishes quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Serve with crusty Italian bread (pane) to scoop up the remaining sauce.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Prepare soffritto: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes until bell peppers soften slightly.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes begin to break down.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until rice grains are translucent around the edges. This is tostatura.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes. The rice should be creamy and al dente (firm to the bite).
Remove pot from heat. Add cold unsalted butter and freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes. This is mantecatura. It creates a creamy, fluid consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 1 minute before serving.
notes: Use high-quality Arborio rice for best results.
Ensure broth is hot when adding to maintain cooking temperature.
Constant stirring is key for creamy risotto.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Kissed Chicken & Picadillo Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of the Coffee-Kissed Chicken & Picadillo Bowl is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, embodying a simple restaurant style. A generous mound of fluffy white rice, subtly flecked with fresh cilantro, forms the base. Beside it, a portion of rich, savory picadillo, a vibrant mix of browned ground beef and pork, small diced yellow onion, bright green peas, and chopped green beans, glistens. Dominating the plate are two pan-seared chicken thighs, their coffee-rubbed skin a deep golden-brown, resting as whole, substantial pieces. A delicate swirl of creamy white lime yogurt sauce artfully drizzles over the chicken and picadillo. A small, neat pile of glossy black beans is placed nearby, adding a contrasting dark hue. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprig of cilantro and a bright green lime wedge. A small side salad of crisp tatsoi and mixed greens, lightly dressed, accompanies the main components. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, creating an inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn or flour tortillas on the side for scooping.
Offer a small bowl of spicy salsa or pickled jalapeños for added heat.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Mix ground coffee, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Rub mixture generously onto chicken. Lightly dust chicken with all-purpose flour. Set aside.

Cook rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Prepare picadillo: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and pork. Brown meat, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced yellow onion and minced garlic to the meat. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened. Stir in diced green beans and green peas. Cook 3 minutes.
Stir in 30g chopped coriander. Season picadillo with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Sear chicken: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and butter in a separate large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and rest.
Deglaze pan: Pour framboise eau de vie into the chicken searing pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Let liquid reduce slightly to form a light sauce. Set aside.
Prepare lime yogurt: In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, juice and zest of 1 lime. Season with a pinch of salt. Mix well.
Prepare black beans: In a small saucepan, gently warm rinsed black beans with a splash of water or vegetable broth. Season with salt.
Prepare salad: Toss tatsoi, salad greens, and chopped parsley with a light vinaigrette (oil, lime juice, salt, pepper).
Assemble bowls: Divide cooked rice among 4 bowls. Spoon picadillo mixture alongside rice. Place chicken thigh next to picadillo.
Add a portion of warm black beans to each bowl. Drizzle lime yogurt over chicken and picadillo. Serve with a side of the fresh green salad and a lime wedge.
notes: For enhanced flavor, marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Savory Cherry Reduction and Avocado Crema
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally featuring a golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast. The chicken is cooked whole, showcasing its succulent interior. A rich, glossy savory cherry reduction is artfully spooned over and around the chicken, creating a deep crimson pool. Beside the chicken, a vibrant green, creamy dollop of avocado crema adds a striking color contrast. A few small, fresh sprigs of thyme or chives are delicately placed atop the chicken for garnish. The colors are natural and balanced: golden chicken, deep red sauce, and bright green crema. The textures are varied, from the tender chicken to the smooth sauce and creamy crema. The plate has appropriate negative space, ensuring a professional yet approachable presentation. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and natural, even lighting that highlights the food's appeal.

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme or chives, for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced red onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in pitted cherries, chicken broth, red wine vinegar, and honey. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce reduces and thickens slightly.
Season cherry reduction with salt and pepper to taste.

For avocado crema: Combine avocados, lime juice, sour cream (or Greek yogurt), and chopped cilantro (if using) in a food processor or blender. Process until smooth and creamy. Season with salt to taste.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

To serve: Place one chicken breast on each plate. Spoon cherry reduction generously over and around the chicken. Add a dollop or swirl of avocado crema beside the chicken. Garnish with fresh thyme or chives.
notes: If using frozen cherries, thaw them slightly before adding to the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Garlic Thyme Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Potato and Garlic Thyme Salad is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Golden-brown roasted potato cubes, 2cm, are casually mounded, their crisped edges and fluffy interiors visible. Interspersed are vibrant red cherry tomato halves and translucent, thinly sliced red onion rings. A glossy olive oil and red wine vinegar dressing coats the components. Finely chopped parsley and fresh thyme leaves are scattered generously, adding green pops of color and texture. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, under warm kitchen light. A casually folded cloth napkin rests nearby, emphasizing a homely atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Fresh Thyme
ingredients.quantity: 2 tablespoons, leaves picked, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss diced potatoes with 30ml olive oil, half of the minced garlic, half of the fresh thyme, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until golden brown and tender. Flip halfway through cooking.

While potatoes roast, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, remaining minced garlic, remaining fresh thyme, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Pour dressing over the warm potato mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Tuscan Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table. Al dente rigatoni forms the base, coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato-basil sauce. Succulent, golden-brown seared chicken chunks (approximately 3-4 cm) are nestled among the pasta. Diced red and yellow bell peppers, roasted until tender with slightly charred edges, add bursts of color and sweetness. Fresh green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the dish, providing a fragrant contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese completes the presentation. The dish exudes warmth and rustic elegance, with natural light highlighting the textures. A simple cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside the plate, emphasizing a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Offer a bowl of extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 2 cm pieces. Toss peppers with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 25ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Mince garlic. Dice red onion. Halve plum tomatoes.
Add remaining 20ml olive oil to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced red onion. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved plum tomatoes, dried oregano, and chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-12 minutes, crushing tomatoes with a spoon, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Return cooked chicken chunks and roasted bell peppers to the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Roughly chop fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the sauce. Reserve some for garnish.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to combine thoroughly. Ensure all ingredients are well coated.
Serve immediately. Garnish each plate with reserved fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Use fresh, ripe plum tomatoes for the best flavor in the sauce.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Herb Roasted Chicken with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, single serving of Herb Roasted Chicken with Root Vegetables sits on a sturdy, well-used ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a warm wooden dining table. A generous portion of golden-brown, roasted chicken, presented as a whole piece (e.g., a thigh and drumstick or a breast portion), is the centerpiece. The chicken skin is crisp, deeply golden, and lightly speckled with dried herbs. Beside the chicken are thick chunks of roasted potatoes, their skins slightly blistered and golden, alongside tender, caramelized carrot chunks and soft, roasted onion wedges. All vegetables show slight charring at the edges, indicating proper roasting. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. A casual cloth napkin and simple, everyday flatware are placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere with a hint of natural clutter in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the roasting pan for family style.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Offer a side of warm crusty bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, mix olive oil, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Rub half of the herb mixture all over the chicken, inside and out.
Place chicken in a large roasting pan.
Cut potatoes, carrots, and onions into 2-3 cm chunks.
Arrange potatoes, carrots, and onions around the chicken in the roasting pan.
Drizzle remaining herb mixture over the vegetables. Toss vegetables to coat evenly.
Pour chicken broth or water into the bottom of the roasting pan.
Roast for 60-80 minutes, or until internal temperature of thickest part of thigh reaches 75°C.
Baste chicken and vegetables halfway through roasting.
Let chicken rest 10 minutes before carving.
Serve chicken with roasted vegetables and pan drippings.
notes: Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C.
Basting helps keep chicken moist and skin crispy.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Gooseberry Oatmeal Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Baked Gooseberry Oatmeal Pudding is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The pudding, scooped from a larger baking dish, forms a soft, irregular mound on the plate, showcasing its comforting, homely texture. The top is a light golden brown, with hints of the soft, slightly burst, translucent green and red gooseberries peeking through. Some oats are visibly tender and plump. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed next to the plate. Lighting is warm and soft, mimicking natural kitchen light. The background is slightly out of focus, showing the subtle warmth of a family kitchen environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Combine oats, sugar, cinnamon, and salt in the baking dish. Stir well.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet mixture over the dry ingredients in the baking dish. Stir gently to combine.
Evenly scatter gooseberries over the oat mixture.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the top is golden and the pudding is set.
Let cool slightly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Olive Relish and Mozzarella Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh rests on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an off-white tone. The chicken skin is visibly crisp and slightly puckered. Adjacent to the chicken is a vibrant, irregular mound of Fermented Tomato-Olive Relish, showcasing diced deep red tomatoes and dark purple-black olive chunks. The relish appears moist and slightly glossy from olive oil. A delicate, irregularly shaped, golden-brown mozzarella crisp leans artfully against the chicken, adding a textural contrast. A few fresh, vibrant green oregano leaves are scattered lightly over the relish and plate, providing a pop of color and natural garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a light, textured stone surface, hinting at natural materials. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly visible in the background. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients. A subtle, out-of-focus green plant element is visible in the background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Dice tomatoes into 1cm pieces. Place in a clean 1-liter jar. Dissolve 15g non-iodized salt in 500ml filtered water. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if available. Seal jar loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate when ready.

Prepare Mozzarella Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Thinly slice or tear fresh mozzarella into irregular pieces. Arrange mozzarella on the prepared baking sheet with space between pieces. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from oven and let cool completely on the sheet; crisps will firm up as they cool.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and dried oregano. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from oven and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Prepare Tomato-Olive Relish: Roughly chop the fermented tomatoes. Drain excess liquid if desired. Roughly chop pitted Kalamata olives. In a small bowl, combine chopped fermented tomatoes and olives. Drizzle with remaining 15ml olive oil. Pick fresh oregano leaves from sprigs and roughly chop. Stir into relish. Season with black pepper to taste. Adjust salt if needed, considering the saltiness of the fermented tomatoes and olives.

Plate Dish: Place one pan-seared chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the Fermented Tomato-Olive Relish alongside the chicken. Lean a Mozzarella Crisp against the chicken or relish. Garnish each plate with a small fresh oregano sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Creamy Dijon Sauce and Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: The pan-seared beef dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A generous mound of fluffy, garlic-infused Basmati rice sits at the center. Beside it, two thick, golden-brown seared beef medallions, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, glisten with a rich, dark crust. A creamy, pale yellow Dijon mustard sauce is artfully drizzled over the beef and partially around the rice, its smooth texture contrasting with the rougher rice grains. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is sprinkled over the beef and sauce, adding a vibrant color pop and freshness. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the quality ingredients and professional execution. A folded cotton napkin and simple modern flatware complete the casual bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Rinse Basmati rice under cold water until water runs clear. Combine rice with 600ml water and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a saucepan. Add 4 minced garlic cloves.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Pat beef sirloin steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add beef steaks to the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Cook to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Remove beef from skillet and transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced shallot and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in Dijon mustard until well combined. Gradually whisk in heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Slice rested beef into thick medallions. Arrange garlic rice on individual plates. Place beef medallions beside the rice. Spoon creamy Dijon sauce generously over the beef and around the rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Beer-Thyme Reduction and Garlic-Herb Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Beer-Thyme Reduction and Garlic-Herb Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick medallions of pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a savory crust, are centrally placed, slightly overlapping. A glossy, amber beer-thyme reduction is spooned generously over the chicken. Alongside, several halved roasted baby potatoes are scattered, their skins slightly crisped and golden. Bright red, roasted cherry tomatoes, gently shriveled, provide bursts of color. A small, creamy dollop of white garlic-herb mayonnaise sits neatly beside the chicken. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing each component to breathe. A fresh thyme sprig garnishes the chicken. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish.
instructions: Prepare Potatoes: Wash potatoes. Halve larger potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast in oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Prepare Cherry Tomatoes: Toss cherry tomatoes with 5ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to baking tray with potatoes for the last 10-15 minutes of roasting.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 10ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven with potatoes for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

Make Beer-Thyme Reduction: Deglaze skillet with beer over medium heat. Scrape up browned bits. Add chicken stock and fresh thyme sprigs. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, reducing liquid by half. Stir in butter until melted and sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Remove thyme sprigs.
Prepare Garlic-Herb Mayonnaise: Mince garlic finely. Chop fresh parsley. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, minced garlic, and chopped parsley. Season with a pinch of salt.

Plate Dish: Slice each chicken breast into thick medallions. Arrange chicken on individual plates. Spoon beer-thyme reduction over chicken. Arrange roasted potatoes and cherry tomatoes beside chicken. Dollop garlic-herb mayonnaise beside the chicken. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig or chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Turkey and Green Bean Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spanish Turkey and Green Bean Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rice is a warm golden-orange hue from saffron and paprika, studded with tender, browned turkey chunks and vibrant, bright green beans. Diced red tomatoes are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color. The rice has a slight al dente texture, with individual grains visible. The turkey is cut into substantial, irregular 2-3 cm chunks, maintaining a rustic yet refined appearance. A light drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on top. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned at the side. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing the ingredients clearly with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer additional lemon wedges on the side.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: pinch (about 0.1 gram), steeped in 30 ml warm water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Season turkey chunks with salt and pepper. Brown turkey on all sides. Remove turkey from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomato and smoked paprika. Cook for 2-3 minutes, pressing tomatoes slightly.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat rice with the sofrito mixture. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in pork stock and steeped saffron. Stir gently. Bring to a simmer.
Return turkey chunks to the pan. Distribute evenly.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add green beans to the pan. Gently stir them into the rice. Re-cover.
Continue cooking for another 8-10 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh parsley and lemon wedges.
notes: Use a wide, shallow pan for best results to ensure even rice cooking.
Avoid over-stirring the rice once the stock is added to prevent stickiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Savory Oat Risotto and Gooseberry Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting portion of Savory Oat Risotto sits centrally on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The creamy, light brown oats are loosely mounded, appearing fluid and inviting. Beside the risotto, two or three thick, pan-seared pork loin medallions, displaying a deep golden-brown crust, are casually placed. A glossy, deep ruby-red gooseberry glaze is artfully drizzled over the pork and slightly onto the risotto, adding a vibrant contrast. Fresh green sprigs of thyme are nestled among the pork and oats for a touch of herbaceous freshness. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded beige cloth napkin and a set of polished everyday flatware complete the homely setting. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the dish. The background is minimally cluttered, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Prepare Gooseberry Glaze: Combine gooseberries, 50ml water, and sugar (if using) in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10-15 minutes until gooseberries soften. Mash with a fork. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Return liquid to saucepan. Simmer until thickened to a glaze consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Sear Pork Loin: Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork loin. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Reduce heat to medium. Cook until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove pork from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, covered loosely with foil.

Cook Savory Oat Risotto: In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and chopped thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add rolled oats. Stir 1 minute to lightly toast.
Pour in 200ml vegetable broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Gradually add remaining broth, 150ml at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed. This will take 15-20 minutes.
Once broth is mostly absorbed and oats are creamy, stir in milk. Cook 2-3 minutes until creamy. Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid.

Assemble and Serve: Slice rested pork loin into thick medallions. Spoon savory oat risotto onto individual plates. Arrange pork medallions beside or slightly on top of the risotto. Drizzle with gooseberry glaze. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Herb Sustainable Salad with Pickled Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm, earthy tone, set against a light, reclaimed wood table surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating gentle shadows. The composition is minimalistic, featuring ample white space around the ingredients. Thinly shredded green cabbage forms a natural base, providing a fresh, crisp texture. Scattered artfully across the cabbage are vibrant components: thinly sliced rounds of bright orange pickled carrots, delicate ruby-red pickled radish slices, and translucent purple slivers of pickled red onion. Small, irregular pieces of finely shredded, pale pickled chicken are interspersed, offering a subtle textural contrast without dominating the visual. Fresh, vibrant green basil and oregano leaves are loosely placed throughout the salad, acting as natural garnishes. The light vinaigrette dressing glistens on the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. The overall presentation is clean, unfussy, and highlights the pure beauty and natural textures of each sustainable ingredient. An undyed linen napkin is folded beside the plate, and a hint of a green plant in a simple pot is visible in the soft-focus background.
instructions: Prepare the pickling liquid: In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, 5 g salt, and peppercorns. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.

Place shredded chicken, sliced carrots, radishes, and red onion in separate non-reactive containers. Pour cooled pickling liquid over each, ensuring vegetables and chicken are fully submerged. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, Dijon mustard, 2 tablespoons of the pickling liquid from the pickled vegetables, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Finely chop half of the fresh basil and oregano leaves. Stir into the dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, combine thinly shredded green cabbage. Drain the pickled carrots, radishes, and red onion. Add them to the cabbage. Drain the pickled chicken and add it to the bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat all components evenly. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Divide the salad among four serving plates. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh basil and oregano leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: To minimize waste, reserve any leftover pickling liquid for future use with other vegetables.
Compost all vegetable scraps and herb stems.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash Pasta with Sage Brown Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash Pasta is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a simple light wood table. The tagliatelle pasta, glistening with sage brown butter sauce, forms a generous mound. Slices of golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cut into 2 cm thick pieces, are arranged naturally atop the pasta. Vibrant orange, roasted butternut squash cubes, approximately 2 cm, are scattered amongst the pasta and chicken, showcasing their caramelized edges. Freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish. A few crispy, dark green sage leaves are artfully placed for garnish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A white cotton napkin and classic silver fork are placed beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and deseed butternut squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss squash cubes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into 2 cm thick pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

In the same skillet used for chicken, melt butter over medium heat. Add whole sage leaves. Cook until butter browns and sage is crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove crispy sage leaves; set aside for garnish. Add minced garlic to the brown butter. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Add chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Add cooked pasta and sliced chicken to the skillet. Toss to coat. If needed, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, to achieve desired consistency. Stir in half of the grated Parmesan.
Divide pasta among four plates. Arrange roasted squash cubes and sliced chicken pieces on top. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and crispy sage leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Chicken Galantine, and Onion Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A refined culinary composition on an elegant, large white bone china plate. In the center, a perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion displays a deep golden-brown crust and succulent, rosy interior. Adjacent, two artfully arranged, thick rounds of chicken galantine reveal a delicate, pale interior flecked with herbs and onion. A generous, fluid swirl of creamy onion risotto anchors the elements, its pearlescent grains glistening. A rich, glossy red wine jus is meticulously spooned around the beef and galantine, creating a sophisticated dark accent. The dish is precisely garnished with golden, crispy shallot rings for textural contrast. Abundant negative space emphasizes minimalist elegance. The setting features a polished grey marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin, and professional, dramatic lighting, creating a luxurious and artistic presentation.
instructions: For the Red Wine Jus:
Reduce red wine in a saucepan over medium heat until almost syrupy.
Add beef stock. Simmer until reduced by half and slightly thickened.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
For the Chicken Galantine:
Carefully butterfly chicken breasts open. Pound lightly to even thickness.
Finely mince 1 shallot and 1 clove garlic. Sauté in a small pan with a teaspoon of olive oil until soft. Cool.
Chop a small portion of chicken trimmings very finely. Mix with sautéed shallot, garlic, 2g chopped thyme, 2g chopped parsley, salt, and pepper.
Spread mixture evenly over butterflied chicken breasts.
Roll chicken tightly into a cylinder. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap, then aluminum foil.
Poach in simmering water for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from water. Chill immediately in ice bath. Once cold, unwrap and slice into 2 cm thick rounds just before serving.
For the Onion Risotto:
Finely dice yellow onion. Mince 1 clove garlic.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, sauté diced onion in 20ml olive oil until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute.
Add Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring continuously. Wait until liquid is mostly absorbed before adding next ladleful.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy but still al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in 30g cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
For the Crispy Shallots:
Thinly slice remaining shallot into rings.
Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan to 160°C.
Fry shallot rings until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Lightly salt.
For the Seared Beef Tenderloin:
Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is achieved.
Add 30g butter and 3g thyme sprigs to pan during last minute. Baste beef with melted butter.
Remove beef from pan. Rest for 5 minutes before serving whole.
To Serve (for 4 portions):
Plate a generous swirl of onion risotto. Arrange one seared beef tenderloin medallion next to it. Place two chicken galantine rounds adjacent.
Spoon red wine jus artfully around the beef and galantine. Garnish with crispy shallot rings.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper & Rice Salad with Herbed Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple wooden table surface. The composition is organized yet organic, with moderate negative space. The base of the salad is fluffy, golden long-grain rice. Roasted bell peppers, cut into tender-crisp 2 cm strips, display vibrant reds, yellows, and oranges, artistically interspersed. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes and crisp 1 cm diced green cucumber add fresh color and texture. Thinly sliced red onion provides a subtle purple accent. Scattered among the vegetables are small, golden-brown cubes of pan-seared chicken breast, showcasing its tender texture. Dark, briny Kalamata olive halves are visible throughout. Crumbled white feta cheese offers a creamy contrast. The entire salad is lightly coated in a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette. A generous sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh green parsley provides a vibrant top garnish. The setting is a modern bistro, with soft, natural, even lighting. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. In the subtle background, a small olive oil cruet and a rustic bread basket suggest traditional Mediterranean dining, without distracting from the dish's central focus.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Add 2 sprigs of thyme to cooking water. Let cool completely.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp. Let cool.

Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt, pepper, and leaves from 1 sprig of thyme. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into 2 cm cubes.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion. Pit and halve Kalamata olives.

For the dressing, finely mince garlic and remaining thyme leaves. In a small bowl, whisk together 50 ml extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, roasted bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, and Kalamata olives. Add diced chicken.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine. Crumble feta cheese over the salad. Roughly chop fresh parsley and sprinkle over the salad. Serve immediately or chill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Giblet Ragout with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Turkey Giblet Ragout with Pappardelle is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Long, wide pappardelle ribbons are loosely swirled, forming a soft mound. The rich, dark reddish-brown ragout is generously spooned over, with sauce and tender giblet chunks cascading. Turkey giblets are diced into rustic 1-2 cm chunks, showing their seared, deep brown exterior. Finely diced mirepoix vegetables integrate into the glossy sauce. Garnish includes a generous scattering of freshly grated, pale yellow Parmesan cheese and vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing contrasting colors and textures. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface, with a white cotton napkin and silver fork beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a soft, blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Clean turkey giblets. Remove any tough membranes or fat. Dice heart and gizzard into 1-2 cm chunks. Dice liver into 1 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced turkey giblets. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove giblets from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is reduced by half.
Return browned giblets to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until giblets are very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Season ragout with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency if needed; simmer uncovered for a thicker sauce.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragout. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in bowls. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Roasted Chicken & Tomato Bowl with Fermented Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of the Sustainable Roasted Chicken & Tomato Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, off-white finish, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The composition is clean and minimalist, emphasizing natural forms and ample negative space. A substantial, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and un-sliced, is positioned slightly off-center on a bed of fluffy, pristine white basmati rice. Alongside the chicken, a cluster of vibrant, plump, blistered red cherry tomatoes adds a burst of color and soft texture. Thinly sliced, pale pink quick pickled red onions are artfully scattered, providing a subtle contrast. Small, deliberate dollops of a creamy, off-white fermented garlic paste are placed on the edge of the rice. A delicate sprinkling of bright green chopped parsley and crumbles of white feta cheese provide natural, unfussy garnishes. The lighting is soft and natural, casting gentle shadows that highlight the textures of each ingredient. An undyed linen napkin in a muted beige tone is subtly visible at the corner. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural plant foliage providing a living element without distraction.
instructions: Prepare quick pickled red onion: Thinly slice red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine white vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Pour hot liquid over sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Rinse basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Cook rice according to package directions. Use a 1:1.5 rice to water ratio. Simmer covered for 12-15 minutes. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Add whole cherry tomatoes and minced fresh garlic to the skillet around the chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F).
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Tomatoes should be softened and slightly blistered.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes before carving or serving whole. Keep tomatoes warm.
To assemble each bowl: Place a generous portion of fluffed rice in the base. Arrange one roasted chicken thigh on top of the rice. Spoon roasted cherry tomatoes alongside the chicken.
Dab small amounts of fermented garlic paste onto the plate. Scatter crumbled feta cheese over the dish. Garnish with quick pickled red onion and fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper and Grilled Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A bed of fresh mixed greens forms the base. Artfully arranged atop the greens are golden-brown diced grilled chicken pieces, vivid red julienned roasted bell pepper strips, crisp green half-moon cucumber slices, firm golden chickpeas, dark pitted Kalamata olives, and creamy white crumbled feta cheese. The components are distributed to showcase their distinct colors and textures, creating a balanced and inviting composition with moderate negative space. A light, glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette lightly coats the ingredients, adding a subtle sheen. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even light, emphasizing the freshness and professional preparation of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Skin should blister. Transfer to a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel and julienne peppers.

Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Grill chicken for 6-8 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest for 5 minutes. Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes.
Prepare vegetables. Slice cucumber into 0.5 cm half-moons. Thinly slice red onion.
Combine vinaigrette ingredients in a small bowl. Whisk well.
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, julienned roasted bell peppers, diced chicken, chickpeas, sliced cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, pitted Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese.
Pour vinaigrette over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among four plates. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Garlic Confit Rice and Seasonal Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a bed of glistening, off-white garlic confit rice. The rice, cooked with golden-hued garlic oil, shows individual grains and scattered soft, pale-yellow confit garlic cloves. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant mound of deep green, sautéed seasonal greens, gently wilted, provides a natural color contrast. A few delicate, irregularly shaped shards of crispy chicken skin are scattered over the dish, adding texture. The presentation is minimalist and clean, set on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The plate sits on a light, natural wood surface.
