instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Dice tomato cores and ends (approx. 150g). Combine with 2g salt. Place in a clean jar, press down to submerge in liquid. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.

Prepare Shrimp & Vegetable Broth: In a pot, combine reserved shrimp shells, mushroom stems, onion skins, carrot peels, and celery ends. Add 1 litre water. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain. Discard solids. Season broth with salt. Keep warm.
Prepare Mushroom Duxelles: Finely dice mushroom caps (150g). Sauté with 1 tbsp olive oil until liquid evaporates and mushrooms are golden. Set aside.
Prepare Chicken: Butterfly each chicken breast. Lightly pound to even thickness. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.

Stuff Chicken: Mix sautéed mushrooms with 50g of the fermented diced tomatoes. Divide mixture evenly. Place filling inside each butterflied chicken breast. Roll tightly. Secure with toothpicks if needed.

Cook Chicken: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer to oven-safe dish. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Cook Shrimp: While chicken bakes, quickly sear peeled shrimp in the same pan for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and cooked through.
Plate: Slice cooked chicken breasts into thick medallions. Place 2-3 medallions per plate. Arrange seared shrimp alongside. Ladle warm shrimp and vegetable broth around the chicken.
Garnish: Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and chives.
notes: Adjust fermentation time based on ambient temperature and desired tanginess.
Use any vegetable scraps for the broth; creativity is encouraged for zero-waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Kvass and Pickled Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously sized, deep-brown braised beef chunk is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone. The beef is richly caramelized on its surface, revealing tender, moist interior textures. Surrounding the beef are several thick, perfectly cooked rounds of vibrant orange carrots and pale parsnips, arranged organically. A natural, glistening dark sauce from the braising liquid pools beneath the beef and vegetables. Alongside, a small, artfully arranged mound of bright crimson pickled beet juliennes adds vibrant color contrast and tang. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting rustic textures and earthy colors. The background is clean and minimalist, showing subtle hints of natural plant elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple boiled or roasted potatoes.
Traditionally accompanied by pickled vegetables (marinované ovoshchi).
Enjoy with dark rye bread.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4 large chunks. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, rye flour, tomato paste, and mustard. Stir well for 1 minute.
Pour in kvass and vegetable broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add bay leaves and peppercorns. Liquid should mostly cover the beef. Add more broth if needed.
Cover pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Peel carrots and parsnips. Cut into 2cm thick rounds. Add to the pot during the last 45 minutes of cooking. Ensure vegetables are submerged.
While beef braises, prepare pickled root vegetables: Peel beets and julienne them.
Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until dissolved.
Place julienned beets and dill into a clean jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over beets. Seal and let cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Once beef is tender, remove from heat. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: Kvass is a traditional fermented rye bread drink, adding authentic sourness and depth.
This recipe utilizes seasonal root vegetables and emphasizes zero-waste principles.
Pickled beets provide a natural tang and are a common Russian accompaniment.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken with Seasonal Root Vegetable Puree and Pickled Radish Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. The plate features a natural, slightly irregular mound of creamy, pale orange root vegetable puree, its texture soft and inviting. Beside it, a whole, golden-brown pan-seared fermented chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, showcasing its natural shape. A small, vibrant cluster of bright green pickled radish greens, with their delicate ruffled edges, is thoughtfully placed to one side, providing a contrasting color and texture. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the elements, emphasizing the pure beauty and natural forms of each ingredient. A few tiny, fresh chive pieces are scattered over the puree and chicken. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and soft, diffused natural lighting, creating an organic, unfussy aesthetic. The background is clean, with subtle hints of natural elements like blurred greenery.
instructions: Combine water, 15g sea salt, 5g sugar, smashed garlic, dill sprigs, and black peppercorns. Stir to dissolve salt and sugar.
Place chicken thighs in a clean jar. Pour brine over chicken. Ensure chicken is fully submerged.
Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Rinse chicken before cooking. Pat chicken dry.
Wash radish greens thoroughly. Roughly chop greens.
In a small saucepan, combine 100ml apple cider vinegar, 100ml water, 10g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour hot pickling liquid over chopped radish greens in a heatproof jar.
Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Boil chopped carrots, parsnips, and potatoes in salted water. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain vegetables well. Return vegetables to pot.
Add chicken stock and butter. Mash or blend until smooth.
Season puree with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear fermented chicken thighs. Cook 5-7 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pan. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Spoon a generous dollop of root vegetable puree onto each plate. Form a natural, organic shape.
Place one whole chicken thigh next to the puree.
Arrange a small portion of pickled radish greens beside the chicken.
Garnish with a few small sprigs of fresh herbs.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing radish greens, which are often discarded. Chicken bones can be used for homemade stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano with Roasted Plantains
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. Two pieces of tender, whole boneless chicken thigh, richly coated in a deep, glossy, reddish-brown mole sauce, are the focal point. The mole sauce has a smooth, thick texture, clinging to the chicken, with visible specks of ground spices. Beside the chicken, three to four thick, diagonal slices of roasted plantain, with golden-brown edges and a soft, caramelized center, are neatly arranged. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh cilantro and a scattering of pale, toasted sesame seeds garnish the chicken and sauce, adding contrasting color and texture. The overall plating is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. A stack of warm corn tortillas rests beside the plate. A simple white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even light, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, featuring soft, blurred restaurant elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the sauce.
Offer a side of Mexican red rice.
instructions: Carefully remove stems and seeds from dried chilies. Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Turn frequently. Do not burn. Transfer to a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
Heat 10 ml oil in a large pot. Add tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, and garlic. Cook until softened and slightly charred, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from pot. Set aside.
In the same dry pan, toast almonds, sesame seeds, tortilla/bread, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, cloves, cinnamon stick, and peppercorns. Toast until fragrant, about 3-5 minutes. Stir constantly.

Drain rehydrated chilies. Reserve soaking liquid. Combine chilies, toasted aromatics, toasted nuts/seeds/bread, chocolate, and 200 ml chicken broth in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Add more broth if needed to blend.

Heat remaining 20 ml oil in the large pot over medium heat. Carefully pour the mole puree into the hot oil. Stir constantly to prevent sticking. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until sauce darkens and thickens. This step is crucial for flavor development.

Gradually whisk in remaining 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and optional sugar to taste. The sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon.

Season chicken thighs with salt. Add chicken to the simmering mole sauce. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Cover. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

While chicken cooks, prepare plantains. Peel plantains. Slice into 1 cm thick diagonal rounds. Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast at 200°C (390°F) for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway. Roast until golden brown and tender.

To serve, place a portion of mole chicken on a plate. Spoon generous amount of mole sauce over chicken. Arrange roasted plantain slices beside the chicken. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Mole sauce improves in flavor the next day. Make ahead for best results.
Adjust chili heat by adding or reducing arbol chilies if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Cheddar Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Garlic Cheddar Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Thick chunks of golden-brown roasted chicken are interspersed with roasted potato wedges. The chicken has a slightly browned exterior and moist interior. Potato wedges show crisp edges and tender centers. A layer of melted, bubbly sharp cheddar cheese covers parts of the dish, displaying warm golden and slightly browned patches. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A casual, folded cloth napkin and standard metal flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, suggesting a homely kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut chicken thighs into thick chunks.
Wash and cut potatoes into large wedges.
Mince garlic cloves.
In a large baking dish, combine chicken chunks, potato wedges, minced garlic, olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients.
Pour chicken broth into the baking dish.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Shred cheddar cheese.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and golden brown.
Chop fresh parsley.
Garnish the bake with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust baking time based on potato size and oven performance.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Cheddar Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Garlic Cheddar Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Thick chunks of golden-brown roasted chicken are interspersed with roasted potato wedges. The chicken has a slightly browned exterior and moist interior. Potato wedges show crisp edges and tender centers. A layer of melted, bubbly sharp cheddar cheese covers parts of the dish, displaying warm golden and slightly browned patches. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A casual, folded cloth napkin and standard metal flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, suggesting a homely kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side for dipping.

Cut chicken thighs into thick chunks.
Wash and cut potatoes into large wedges.
Mince garlic cloves.

Shred cheddar cheese.

Return to oven and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and golden brown.
Chop fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Layered Summer Vegetable Timbale
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Layered Summer Vegetable Timbale is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The timbale is a vibrant cylinder, 7-8 cm diameter, 5-6 cm high. Thin, roasted rounds of eggplant, zucchini, yellow squash, and red tomato are meticulously layered vertically in an overlapping circular pattern, showcasing their distinct colors: deep purple, bright green, sunny yellow, and rich red. Vegetables retain shape with slight char, indicating tender-crisp texture. A rustic tomato confit base fills the center. A delicate balsamic glaze sweeps the plate. Fresh parsley sprigs garnish the top. Ample negative space highlights the dish. The setting is a modern bistro: simple light wooden table, white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting creates a professional, approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light main course.
Accompanied by crusty baguette or artisanal bread.
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Slice eggplant, zucchini, and yellow squash into 5 mm thick rounds. Slice tomatoes into 5 mm thick rounds. Dice onion and bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Lightly brush eggplant, zucchini, and yellow squash rounds with olive oil. Arrange on baking sheets. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast vegetables for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp. Do not overcook. Set aside.
Prepare tomato confit base: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth. Add thyme and rosemary sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Remove herb sprigs.

Assemble timbales: For each serving, use a 7-8 cm diameter ring mold. Stand roasted eggplant, zucchini, yellow squash, and tomato slices alternately in a circular pattern inside the mold, slightly overlapping, creating a layered effect.
Carefully spoon a portion of the tomato confit base into the center of the vegetable layers within the mold.
Gently press down to compact. Carefully lift the ring mold.
Repeat for remaining servings.
notes: Ensure vegetables are sliced uniformly for even roasting and elegant presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Cheesy Cauliflower Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Hearty Beef and Cheesy Cauliflower Shepherd's Pie is presented in a rustic, oval ceramic baking dish, showcasing its comforting, homemade appeal. The top layer of cauliflower mash is a warm golden brown with scattered darker, crispy peaks from the melted cheddar cheese, which forms a delicate crust. Underneath, the rich, savory ground beef mixture, cooked with diced onion, minced garlic, and tomato-infused beef broth, peeks out slightly at the edges, revealing its deep brown hue. The textures are inviting: a creamy, smooth cauliflower mash contrasting with the hearty, slightly chunky beef base. A sparse scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley sits atop the golden crust, providing a fresh accent. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A simple ceramic dinner plate and standard metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the baking dish, along with a casually folded cloth napkin, emphasizing a homely family meal setting. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, focusing entirely on the comforting appeal of the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut cauliflower into florets. Steam or boil until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
While cauliflower cooks, heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the skillet. Break it apart and brown thoroughly, stirring occasionally. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in tomato paste and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing liquid to reduce slightly. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Transfer the beef mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet. Spread evenly.

Return drained cauliflower to the pot. Mash thoroughly until smooth. Stir in sour cream, 100 g of grated cheddar cheese, and the large egg until well combined and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper.
Carefully spoon the cheesy cauliflower mash over the beef mixture, spreading it evenly to cover completely.
Sprinkle the remaining 50 g of grated cheddar cheese over the top of the cauliflower mash.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbly. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C for beef.
Remove from oven and let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Curd Fritters with Seasonal Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone. Three to four irregularly shaped, golden-brown fritters, lightly puffed, are arranged naturally on one side. Beside them, a generous dollop of vibrant, naturally colored berry compote showcases whole and slightly burst seasonal berries, glistening with natural sweetness. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing ample negative space. A single small sprig of fresh mint or a few tiny edible flowers adds a delicate pop of natural green or color. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with a subtle hint of green foliage, emphasizing sustainability and the dish's inherent beauty.

ingredients.name: Seasonal mixed berries (fresh or slightly overripe)
Fresh mint sprigs or edible flowers

instructions: Place fresh cheese curd in a bowl. For a subtle tang, let it sit at room temperature for 1-2 hours, if desired.

In a small saucepan, combine berries, 50 ml maple/date syrup, and lemon juice. Simmer over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly. Mash lightly if desired. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine the cheese curd, flour, egg, 30 ml maple/date syrup, baking powder, and salt. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Heat cooking oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls (about 30 ml each) of batter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly with the back of a spoon.
Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Work in batches if necessary.
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with a reusable cloth or paper towel to drain excess oil.
Arrange 3-4 fritters on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of berry compote alongside. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig or a few edible flowers. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Braised Beef and Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rustic Braised Beef and Chicken is centrally presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Rich, dark reddish-brown sauce coats tender 4-5 cm chunks of braised beef and golden-brown 4-5 cm pieces of chicken. Large, soft 3-4 cm potato wedges are nestled among the meats. The sauce is thick and glossy, with visible flecks of roughly chopped onion and tomato. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh, aromatic contrast. The composition is natural and unforced, allowing moderate negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Traditional, simple European-style flatware (fork and knife) is placed on the napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere with warm, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping in the sauce.
A side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Sear chicken in batches until golden-brown. Remove and set aside. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature during cooking or reheating.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add seared chicken and potato wedges to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue simmering, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Chicken with Tomatoes and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Baked Chicken with Tomatoes and Potatoes is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a subtle, rustic rim. A golden-brown, roasted bone-in chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, rests as the centerpiece. Around it, thick-cut roasted potato wedges, tender and lightly browned, are nestled amongst halved cherry tomatoes that have burst slightly from the heat, releasing their vibrant red juices. Roughly chopped red onion pieces and whole garlic cloves are caramelized and tender, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The components are arranged naturally, overlapping slightly, giving a comforting, homemade appearance. The plate sits on a well-worn, dark wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural light. A folded linen napkin and a simple fork rest beside the plate, completing the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Enjoy family-style directly from the baking dish at the center of the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
In a large baking dish, combine potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped onions, and whole garlic cloves.
Drizzle vegetables with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange seasoned chicken pieces among the vegetables in the baking dish.
Pour chicken broth over the ingredients.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and lightly browned.
Baste chicken and vegetables occasionally during baking.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spanish Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented on a simple, well-used ceramic plate. A generous portion of golden-hued rice, infused with tomato and paprika, forms the base. Nestled atop the rice are two succulent, bone-in chicken thighs, seared to a rich golden-brown. Vibrant red bell pepper slices and small diced onion pieces are visible throughout the rice, adding color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The plating is natural and casual, with components slightly overlapping, as if served directly from a family skillet. The scene is set on a warm, rustic wooden table with natural lighting, evoking a homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet for a communal dining experience.
Offer crusty bread on the side for soaking up juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and sliced red bell pepper to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, and saffron (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and their juice. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring to coat rice.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Tomato, Mushroom, and Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Skillet Chicken with Tomato, Mushroom, and Bell Pepper Pasta is presented on a round, white ceramic plate. The plate is positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A generous mound of al dente penne pasta, coated in a rustic red tomato sauce, is piled on one side of the plate. Interspersed within the pasta are tender, slightly browned slices of mushroom, vibrant diced bell peppers in red and green, and soft, sweet diced onion. Several golden-brown, thick chunks of seared chicken breast are nestled beside the pasta. The dish is generously topped with melted, creamy mozzarella cheese and a sprinkling of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. Natural light illuminates the scene from kitchen fixtures, creating a warm, inviting glow. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware rest casually beside the plate, completing the authentic, lived-in family meal atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the natural portions.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced bell peppers, and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in diced tomatoes, dried oregano, chicken broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to combine.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet with the pasta. Gently mix.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with shredded mozzarella cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Apple Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, single serving of Creamy Chicken and Apple Pasta is presented on a simple, rustic off-white ceramic plate. The penne pasta is generously coated in a creamy, light beige sauce, mixed with irregular 2 cm cubes of pan-seared golden-brown chicken and tender, small 1 cm cubes of sautéed apple. The components are naturally intertwined, showcasing the comforting textures. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast and fresh aroma. The plate is casually centered on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded, muted plaid cloth napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the homely, satisfying nature of the dish. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen, slightly out of focus, maintaining focus on the hearty meal.
instructions: Cook penne pasta according to package directions. Drain. Reserve 60 ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add cubed chicken. Cook for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion into small pieces. Dice apple into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion to the same skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced apple. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta and cooked chicken back to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tori Jagaimo Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy soup is presented in a deep, rounded white porcelain bowl, reflecting a clean Japanese comfort food style. The soup is fluid and rich, with tender chicken cubes (2-3 cm) and small potato chunks (2 cm) visible beneath the surface. Small pasta shapes are evenly distributed throughout. A vibrant scattering of bright green, thinly sliced green onions provides a fresh contrast on top, complemented by a very light dusting of reddish-orange Shichimi Togarashi. The chicken is cooked through and retains its cubed shape. Potatoes are soft but hold their form. The overall color is a warm, creamy off-white with subtle hints of orange from carrots and vibrant green from the garnish. The bowl is placed slightly off-center on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded, light grey cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. The setting suggests a modern bistro, with soft, natural, even lighting illuminating the dish from above and slightly to the side, creating gentle shadows that add depth without harshness. The scene is uncluttered, focusing entirely on the soup as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: This comforting soup is often served as a main dish in Japanese homes.
Sometimes served alongside a small portion of steamed white rice or a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Mild melting cheese (Fontina or mild Cheddar)

instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice onion and carrot finely. Mince garlic. Cube chicken into 2-3 cm pieces. Cube potatoes into 2 cm pieces.
Heat butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and carrot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes. Cook until lightly browned on all sides.
Sprinkle flour over chicken and vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Gradually whisk in dashi stock to create a smooth base. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato cubes. Simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Add pasta. Cook according to package directions, typically 8-10 minutes, until al dente.
Pour in milk. Stir gently.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheese until melted and incorporated.
Season with soy sauce, mirin, salt, and white pepper. Adjust to taste.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and a pinch of Shichimi Togarashi if desired.
notes: This recipe adapts Western-style cream soup elements with Japanese flavors and ingredients, creating a comforting 'yoshoku' (Western-style Japanese food) dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peruvian Arroz con Pollo is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing vibrant colors and textures. Two golden-brown, seared chicken pieces, a thigh and a drumstick, are prominently nestled atop a generous bed of fluffy, emerald-green rice. The rice is infused with cilantro, speckled with bright red diced bell pepper and tender green peas, and small diced carrots. The chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the dish as a garnish, adding a burst of fresh green. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich hues and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Salsa Criolla (sliced red onion, aji limo, lime juice, and cilantro).
Pair with a glass of Chicha Morada or Inca Kola.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do this in batches to avoid crowding the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced red onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in aji amarillo paste, cumin powder, and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
In a blender, combine fresh cilantro with 100 ml of chicken broth. Blend until smooth to create a vibrant green cilantro paste.
Add rice to the pot with the cooked aromatics. Stir to coat the rice, toasting for 2 minutes.
Pour in the dark beer (or chicken broth) and remaining chicken broth. Stir in the cilantro paste. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in frozen green peas and small diced carrots. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving. Check chicken internal temperature, it should be 75°C (167°F).
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is served in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl, artfully mounded but with a natural, free-flowing consistency. The risotto, a pale creamy hue, is speckled with golden-brown diced chicken pieces (2 cm cubes) and earthy, sliced cremini mushrooms. Scattered generously over the top are vibrant red, slightly blistered halved cherry tomatoes. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed as a garnish, along with a delicate drizzle of golden olive oil. The composition is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the risotto. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background to maintain focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to 'fare la scarpetta' (mop up remaining risotto).
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and blistered.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into 2 cm cubes.
Slice mushrooms. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Sauté mushrooms until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt. Set aside.

Finely dice shallot. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 grams butter over medium heat. Add shallot. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast rice kernels.

Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed. Gradually add hot chicken stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20-25 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and rice al dente.
Stir in diced chicken and sautéed mushrooms during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Continue adding stock until desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 grams butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously for 1 minute for 'mantecatura' (creamy finish). Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Top with roasted cherry tomatoes and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken stock is hot when added to the rice to maintain cooking temperature.
Risotto should be stirred constantly for creaminess and even cooking.
The final consistency should be fluid, allowing the risotto to spread slightly on the plate.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (finishing the risotto with butter and cheese for a creamy texture)

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork & Mustard Mash Broth Bowl
recipes.special_requests: You need to use pork tenderloin  Potatoes should be in the form of mashed potatoes, mustard paste should be added there.  pork should be toasted with a crust.  You can add green onions, soy sauce, honey to the dish. cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single, comforting portion of Seared Pork & Mustard Mash Broth Bowl is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The clear, amber broth cradles thick medallions of seared pork tenderloin, showing a golden-brown crust. A creamy, pale yellow dollop of mustard mashed potatoes sits beside the pork, contrasting textures. Vibrant green chopped green onions and fresh thyme sprigs garnish the dish. The plating is casual, asymmetrical, and natural, fitting a homely family meal. A simple spoon rests nearby, with a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in atmosphere. The entire bowl is visible, showcasing the hearty, comforting dish with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork tenderloin 3-4 minutes per side until a golden-brown crust forms. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove pork, set aside to rest. Slice into 2 cm thick medallions.
Peel and dice onion. In the same pan, add a knob of butter. Sauté diced onion over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock, soy sauce, and honey. Add chili flakes and two thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 10 minutes to meld flavors.
While broth simmers, peel and quarter potatoes. Place potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes well. Return to the hot pot. Add remaining butter and Dijon mustard. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

To serve, ladle hot broth into individual bowls. Arrange sliced pork medallions in the broth. Place a generous dollop of mustard mashed potatoes next to the pork. Garnish with chopped green onions and remaining fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure pork is cooked through for safety.
Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken & Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Mexican Chicken & Rice Skillet is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. A generous mound of vibrant, reddish-orange rice, cooked to a tender fluffiness, forms the center. The rice is visibly studded with bright yellow corn kernels, dark black beans, and soft, off-white potato cubes, all evenly distributed. Two substantial, golden-brown seared chicken thigh pieces, whole and unsliced, rest prominently on top of the rice. A generous sprinkle of freshly chopped green cilantro provides a vibrant contrast. A quartered lime wedge sits beside the dish. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's inviting textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, and the background is minimal and subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of salsa fresca or pico de gallo.
A small bowl of crema or sour cream can be offered.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Pickled jalapeño chilies, sliced or diced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, scraping up any browned bits from bottom of skillet.
Add rice to skillet. Stir to coat rice in tomato mixture.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add diced potatoes, black beans, corn kernels, and pickled jalapeños. Stir gently to combine.
Return seared chicken thighs to skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Pork Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Beef and Pork Pasta Bake is presented as a generous, cleanly cut rectangular portion on a pristine white porcelain plate. The golden-brown potato gratin topping, achieved through thin, overlapping slices, boasts a crisp, slightly caramelized surface. Below, the rich, deep red-brown meat sauce, brimming with tender ground beef and pork, is visible, interspersed with al dente penne pasta. Finely diced carrots and onions add subtle flecks of orange and white within the savory sauce. A light drizzle of creamy béchamel sauce peeks from beneath the potatoes. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, offering a fresh contrast. The plate sits on a warm, natural wood bistro table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting textures and inviting colors.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and pork. Brown thoroughly, breaking up meat with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, hot sauce, soy sauce, allspice, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for at least 60 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt to taste.
While meat sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.

In a separate saucepan, melt 50 g butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1-2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened. Remove from heat. Whisk in egg yolk, nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a large baking dish (approx. 20x30 cm).
Combine drained pasta with the meat sauce. Mix well. Spread evenly into the prepared baking dish.
Pour béchamel sauce over the pasta and meat mixture, spreading evenly.
Arrange thinly sliced potatoes over the béchamel in an overlapping pattern. Brush melted butter over the potatoes. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese if using.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and tender, and the sauce is bubbly. If potatoes brown too quickly, loosely cover with foil.
Let the bake rest for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Ensure internal temperature of meat reaches 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single baked chicken breast sits on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The chicken is topped with a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese, beneath which a creamy, baked mayonnaise layer is visible. Tender, softened rounds of red tomato are nestled into the cheese and mayonnaise. The chicken itself is presented as a whole piece, or in 2-3 thick, natural chunks. Thinly sliced, translucent onion half-moons form a soft bed underneath the chicken, their edges slightly caramelized. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a touch of color. The plate is adequately filled, showcasing a modest, homely portion. The ceramic plate, with its subtle imperfections, rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A folded, plain linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, characteristic of a cozy kitchen or dining area. The background is soft and unobtrusive, hinting at a lived-in, family kitchen atmosphere with everyday flatware visible.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Lightly grease a large baking dish with olive oil.
Spread the thinly sliced onion evenly across the bottom of the baking dish.
Season chicken breasts with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder on both sides.
Place the seasoned chicken breasts over the onion slices in the baking dish.
Evenly spread mayonnaise over the top of each chicken breast.
Arrange the sliced tomato rounds over the mayonnaise layer on each chicken breast.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese generously over the tomatoes and chicken.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the cheese is golden brown and bubbling.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, centered on a worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table. The stew features chunky, golden-brown seared chicken pieces nestled amongst soft, diced zucchini, celery, and onion, all coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. Flecks of dried herbs are visible. A generous spoonful of fresh, finely diced cucumber and chopped parsley relish sits atop the stew, providing a vibrant green and white textural contrast. The plate below the bowl is a simple, everyday ceramic. A casually folded beige linen napkin and basic metal flatware rest beside the bowl. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating an inviting, unpretentious family meal atmosphere. The focus is on comfort and natural appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the stew's sauce.
A side of plain white rice can be served to soak up the broth.
The fresh cucumber relish provides a cooling and bright contrast to the hearty stew.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, celery, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in diced zucchini, canned diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While stew simmers, prepare the relish: In a small bowl, combine finely diced cucumber, half of the chopped fresh parsley, red wine vinegar, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Season stew with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with the remaining fresh parsley and a generous spoonful of the cucumber relish on top.
notes: For best flavor, allow the stew to rest for 10 minutes before serving.
This stew can be made ahead and reheats well.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken and Egg Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Classic Chicken and Egg Fried Rice is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular, handcrafted feel, showcasing its comforting, homely appeal. The rice is a warm, golden-brown hue, speckled throughout with fluffy, scrambled egg pieces and tender, bite-sized chunks of pan-seared chicken. The grains of rice are separate and glistening, indicating proper stir-frying. Beside the bowl, a small pile of fresh, thinly sliced cucumber batons provides a refreshing contrast. A light sprinkle of finely chopped spring onions garnishes the top of the fried rice. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in soft, warm light from an overhead kitchen fixture. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin. The scene is unpretentious, capturing a casual, family kitchen dining moment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks
Offer a side of chili oil for extra heat

ingredients.name: Spring onions, chopped (white and green parts separated)

instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2cm chunks.
Heat 5ml vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned.

Pour in 50ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and stock is mostly absorbed. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Whisk 2 eggs with a pinch of salt. Add 5ml vegetable oil to the hot pan. Pour in whisked eggs. Scramble until just set. Remove eggs. Break into small pieces. Set aside.
Add remaining 5ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add cooked rice to the pan. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry 2-3 minutes, ensuring rice is heated through and slightly toasted.
Return cooked chicken and scrambled egg to the pan. Add white parts of chopped spring onions.
Pour in 15ml soy sauce and 5ml sesame oil. Stir-fry everything together for 2-3 minutes until well combined and heated through.
Slice cucumber into thin batons (julienne).
Serve fried rice immediately in a bowl. Garnish with green parts of spring onions and fresh cucumber batons on the side.
notes: Using day-old, cold rice is crucial for good fried rice as it prevents stickiness and allows for separate grains.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Tomato Paella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Tomato Paella is presented in a shallow, wide white ceramic plate, reminiscent of a paella pan. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled among saffron-infused Bomba rice. The rice displays a vibrant yellow-orange hue, interspersed with thin strips of bright red and green bell peppers and small, diced pieces of cooked tomato. A visible, slightly crispy layer of socarrat peeks from beneath the rice. The dish showcases varied textures: tender chicken, firm individual rice grains, and soft vegetables. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the top, and a vibrant yellow lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white porcelain plate, standard flatware, and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting to create a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan at the table for a traditional experience.
Offer crusty bread to sop up any remaining juices.
Serve with additional lemon wedges for squeezing over individual portions.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes, grated or finely diced

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a 30 cm paella pan or large, shallow skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in minced garlic, grated tomatoes, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. This is the sofrito.
Add Bomba rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice evenly with the sofrito. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pan, distributing evenly.
Pour hot chicken broth over the rice and chicken. Do not stir after adding broth.

Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is nearly cooked. Do not stir during this phase to allow socarrat to form.
If rice is still hard, add a little more hot broth, 50 ml at a time. Continue simmering until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Once liquid is absorbed, increase heat to medium-high for 1-2 minutes to create a crispy bottom layer (socarrat). Listen for crackling sounds. Be careful not to burn.
Remove paella from heat. Cover with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
traditional_techniques: Socarrat formation (crispy rice crust at the bottom of the pan)

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Roasted Chicken with Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, crispy golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. Around it, golden-edged roasted potato wedges are artfully arranged, showcasing their fluffy interior. Several unpeeled, lightly caramelized garlic cloves are nestled among the potatoes. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The textures are prominent: crispy chicken skin, tender chicken meat, and firm yet yielding potatoes with a slightly charred exterior. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table with a soft cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut new potatoes into halves or quarters, creating wedges or chunky pieces.
Lightly smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife, leaving them unpeeled.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, smashed garlic, olive oil, picked rosemary leaves, and picked thyme leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange the seasoned potatoes and garlic in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place the seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among the potatoes on the baking tray.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
If desired, during the last 10 minutes, you may add 100ml chicken stock to the pan to create a light pan sauce.
Remove from oven. Squeeze half a lemon over the chicken and potatoes. Cut the remaining lemon half into wedges for serving.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage, Roasted Tomato, and Orange Salad with Herb-Infused Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on an earthy-toned handcrafted ceramic plate. Thinly shredded, pale green fermented cabbage forms the base. Vibrant red-orange roasted cherry tomato halves, slightly wrinkled, are scattered throughout. Bright orange segments, glistening with juice, are interspersed. Small, tender pieces of herb-infused shredded chicken are thoughtfully placed, ensuring a vegetable-forward focus. Freshly chopped green parsley and mint are sprinkled for verdant accents. A light, glistening orange vinaigrette coats all components, enhancing natural colors. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with each ingredient distinctly visible. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood table, with a simple, undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish against a minimalist background.

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast, shredded or finely diced

instructions: Prepare fermented cabbage: Place shredded cabbage in a clean bowl. Sprinkle with sea salt. Massage cabbage for 5-10 minutes until it releases liquid and softens. Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down to ensure cabbage is submerged in its own brine. Cover loosely with a lid or fermentation weight. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in the refrigerator.

Roast tomatoes: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss halved cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized. Let cool.
Prepare chicken: If using raw chicken, poach or roast chicken breast until cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Shred or finely dice. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, olive oil, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of orange zest. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine fermented cabbage, roasted cherry tomatoes, orange segments, shredded chicken, chopped parsley, and chopped mint. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Nashville Hot Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single piece of crispy, deep reddish-orange Nashville Hot Chicken, a boneless skin-on thigh, is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken has a visibly textured, craggy crust from the dredge and a glossy sheen from the chili-infused hot oil coating. Its vibrant color stands out against the white plate. To the side, two soft slices of plain white bread are neatly stacked, and a small, vibrant green pile of thinly sliced dill pickles adds a contrasting color and fresh element. The overall presentation is simple and rustic, honoring its Southern American origins. The plate rests on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded grey cotton napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting from the side highlights the chicken's texture. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, welcoming bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain white bread to soak up the spicy oil.
Serve with dill pickle slices to cut through the richness and heat.
instructions: Combine buttermilk, 10g salt, and 5g black pepper in a bowl. Add chicken thighs. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or up to 12 hours.
In a shallow dish, whisk together flour, 5g salt, 5g black pepper, 15g paprika, 10g garlic powder, 5g onion powder, and 5g cayenne pepper. This is your dredge.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, allowing excess to drip off. Do not rinse. Dredge each chicken thigh in the flour mixture, pressing firmly to coat completely. Shake off excess flour.

Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or deep fryer to 175°C. Carefully lower chicken thighs into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot. Fry chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and crust is golden brown and crispy. Cook in batches if necessary.
Remove cooked chicken to a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain. Reserve 250 ml of the hot frying oil.
In a heatproof bowl, combine the reserved hot frying oil with 60g cayenne pepper, 30g brown sugar, 5g paprika, 10g garlic powder, and the 50 ml hot sauce. Whisk until smooth.
Brush or spoon the hot oil mixture generously over each piece of fried chicken, ensuring full coverage.
Serve immediately with white bread slices and dill pickle slices.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust cayenne pepper in the hot oil mixture to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Sausage with Mustard Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a rustic, light-toned wooden table surface. A generous, creamy mound of pale yellow mustard mashed potatoes anchors the left side of the plate. To its right, two substantial, golden-brown roasted chicken chunks and one whole, richly browned pork sausage are arranged thoughtfully. A glistening heap of deep amber caramelized onions is spooned artfully over the chicken and sausage, creating a rich contrast. Fine strands of melted, slightly golden cheddar cheese are delicately draped over the meat and onions, catching the light. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is balanced and approachable, with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware is neatly placed beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and warm colors. The background is simple and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Place peeled and quartered potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Return drained potatoes to the hot pot. Add milk, butter, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Mash until smooth and creamy. Keep warm.

Heat 30 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-35 minutes until deep golden brown and very soft. Stir in balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper for the last 5 minutes. Keep warm.

While onions caramelize, heat 5 ml olive oil in a separate large pan over medium heat. Add pork sausages. Cook, turning occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until browned all over and cooked through. Remove from pan and keep warm.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes. Cut each thigh into 2-3 thick chunks.

For each serving, spoon a generous mound of mustard mash onto a white dinner plate. Arrange 2-3 chicken chunks and one whole cooked sausage next to the mash. Spoon a portion of caramelized onions over the chicken and sausage. Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese over the meat and onions. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use good quality, starchy potatoes for the mash.
Caramelizing onions properly takes time; do not rush this step for maximum flavor.
Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Potato Medley with Creamy Cheesy Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of comforting food is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. Two roasted chicken thighs, with crispy golden-brown skin, are placed on one side. Several thick-cut roasted potato wedges, golden and tender, nestle against the chicken. A generous scoop of creamy cheesy orzo pasta, with its small grains in a rich, pale yellow sauce, fills the plate's remaining space, casually touching other components. Fresh, chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The scene is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, suggesting a family kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and basic flatware rest casually beside the plate. Warm, soft light illuminates the food, creating a cozy atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in dining area, focusing on the comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Trim excess skin if desired.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2 cm thick wedges.
In a large bowl, toss chicken and potato wedges with olive oil, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Ensure even coating.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
While chicken and potatoes roast, prepare orzo. Bring chicken broth to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Add orzo to boiling broth. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until orzo is al dente and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir in milk and shredded cheddar cheese into the orzo. Cook, stirring, until cheese is melted and sauce is creamy.
Remove roasted chicken and potatoes from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken thighs and potato wedges alongside creamy cheesy orzo. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken and Apple Curry
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a generous single portion of rich Indian Chicken and Apple Curry. The curry features tender, 3-4 cm chunks of chicken and potato, swimming in a vibrant, reddish-orange sauce. The sauce has a glossy sheen from the oil and is visibly thick, clinging to the ingredients. Small, soft 1 cm apple pieces are subtly integrated, adding a delicate texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro leaves, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. Beside the bowl, a small white bowl of fluffy basmati rice is perfectly portioned. A piece of warm, golden-brown naan bread is folded and placed neatly next to the rice. A traditional metal spoon rests beside the curry bowl. A folded white cotton napkin completes the setting. The scene is bathed in soft, even natural light, highlighting the curry's appealing colors and textures with moderate negative space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy Basmati rice.
Accompany with warm naan bread or roti for scooping the curry.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and mint) or a simple kachumber salad.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or similar), peeled
Apple (e.g., Gala or Fuji), peeled, cored
Chili powder (or Kashmiri chili for color)

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. Stir often.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and chili powder. Stir for 30 seconds until aromatic. Do not burn spices.
Add crushed tomatoes and salt. Stir well. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and oil separates.
Add chicken chunks and potato chunks to the pot. Stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water or chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add diced apple. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Stir in garam masala. Cook for 1 minute.
Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: For best flavor, allow the curry to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving.
This dish pairs well with plain basmati rice or naan bread.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Braised Chicken with Aged Kimchi
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Gochujang Braised Chicken sits centered in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a rustic, unglazed exterior and a smooth, off-white interior. The chicken, a whole bone-in thigh, is rich reddish-brown from the gochujang braise, showcasing its natural, slightly textured skin. Tender, pale daikon cubes are nestled around the chicken. Vibrant, deep red strands of aged kimchi are artfully arranged beside the chicken, adding a burst of color and fermented texture. The glossy, savory braising liquid pools beneath the ingredients. A light scattering of thinly sliced bright green spring onions and a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds garnish the dish. A very fine dusting of grated aged cheese, almost imperceptible, adds a subtle sheen. The plating is minimalist, emphasizing natural forms and colors. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a pair of simple wooden chopsticks and a small, complementary ceramic dish for banchan. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the dish's organic beauty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed white rice.
Offer a variety of small banchan (side dishes) such as pickled cucumbers or seasoned spinach.
Eat with chopsticks and a spoon for the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in the pot. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Add daikon cubes around the chicken.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add chopped aged kimchi to the pot. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and daikon is tender.
Stir in sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot.
notes: To make chicken stock from scratch, simmer chicken bones (from this recipe or saved) with vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends) for 1-2 hours. Strain before use.
Aged kimchi provides deeper flavor; use store-bought or homemade.
The small amount of aged cheese adds an umami depth without overpowering the Korean flavors, aligning with modern sustainable culinary practices that value ingredient quality and minimal waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Chicken with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Mustard Chicken with Rice is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A golden-brown, seared bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh is centered on a bed of fluffy, white Basmati rice. The chicken skin is visibly crisp. A rich, creamy, pale yellow mustard sauce generously coats the chicken and pools around the rice. Small flecks of red chili flakes are visible in the sauce. The diced brown onion pieces are tender and integrated into the sauce. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The overall arrangement is natural and comforting, with components touching. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests casually beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family dining area. The background is minimal, focusing on the homely atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in Dijon mustard, whole grain mustard, and red chili flakes. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rice according to package directions.
Serve chicken thighs over cooked rice. Spoon generous amounts of creamy mustard sauce over chicken and rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Coca-Cola Braised Chicken with Creamed Tatsoi and Apple-Cherry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coca-Cola braised chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table. The chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening from a quick broil, sits prominently. Its skin is lightly crisp, contrasting with the tender, dark meat. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of vibrant green creamed tatsoi offers a soft, inviting texture. A rich, dark brown Coca-Cola reduction sauce is drizzled artfully over the chicken and around the plate. A spoonful of glossy apple-cherry gastrique, showcasing visible diced apple pieces and whole cherries, provides a bright, contrasting color and texture element. The overall composition is balanced and professional, with thoughtful negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin rest beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting from a modern bistro setting. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear briefly on the other side, about 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in Coca-Cola, 150 ml brewed black tea, 30 ml coconut vinegar, and half the lemon juice. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
