Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure liquid mostly covers chicken. If not, add a little water or more tea. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C. Braise for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and is very tender.

While chicken braises, prepare the apple-cherry gastrique. In a small saucepan, combine diced apple, pitted cherries, 30 g granulated sugar, remaining 50 ml brewed black tea, 15 ml coconut vinegar, and remaining lemon juice. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.

Prepare creamed tatsoi. In a separate saucepan, melt 30 g butter over medium heat. Whisk in 30 g flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in 200 ml milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 3-5 minutes. Stir in cream cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Add tatsoi leaves and stir until wilted and coated, about 2-3 minutes. Keep warm.

Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Carefully remove chicken to a plate. Tent with foil. Place the pan with braising liquid on the stovetop over high heat. Reduce liquid by half until it thickens into a glossy sauce, about 8-12 minutes.

Preheat broiler. Whisk egg white lightly. Brush a thin layer of egg white onto the chicken skin. Place chicken under broiler for 1-2 minutes, watching carefully, until skin is lightly crisp and golden. Do not burn.

Plate immediately. Place a portion of creamed tatsoi. Arrange one chicken thigh beside it. Spoon reduced Coca-Cola sauce generously over the chicken. Add a dollop of apple-cherry gastrique beside the chicken and tatsoi. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh lemon zest.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The egg white step helps achieve a lightly crisp, glazed skin on the braised chicken, enhancing visual appeal and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage and Citrus Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, resting on a light-colored reclaimed wood surface. A generous mound of pale green, finely shredded fermented cabbage forms the base. Vibrant orange segments are artfully interspersed, their juicy texture contrasting with the crisp cabbage. Bright yellow-orange passion fruit pulp, with its distinct black seeds, adds pops of color and visual interest. Thinly sliced crimson radishes provide sharp, circular accents, while delicate, translucent shavings of white fennel are gracefully scattered throughout. The dressing, a light sheen of reduced 7 Up and olive oil, lightly coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural luster. The plating is minimalistic and unforced, allowing ample negative space to highlight the individual beauty of each ingredient. A few fresh mint leaves or scattered lime zest provide a subtle, natural garnish. The scene is bathed in soft, natural light, with a clean, unobtrusive background featuring a hint of a green plant. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed nearby, completing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare 7 Up Reduction: Pour 7 Up into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until reduced by half and slightly syrupy, about 5-7 minutes. Let cool.
Prepare Citrus: Segment oranges. Juice limes. Scoop passion fruit pulp. Zest one orange and one lime; set zests aside.
Prepare Vegetables: Thinly slice radishes. Using a mandoline or sharp knife, shave fennel bulb very thinly.
Make Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the cooled 7 Up reduction, fresh lime juice (from 1 lime), extra virgin olive oil, reserved orange zest, sea salt, and black pepper.
Assemble Salad: In a large mixing bowl, gently combine the drained lacto-fermented cabbage, orange segments, passion fruit pulp, thinly sliced radishes, and shaved fennel.

Dress and Serve: Pour the prepared dressing over the salad mixture. Gently toss to coat all ingredients evenly. Divide the salad among four plates. Garnish with fresh mint leaves or reserved lime zest, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken, Potatoes, and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken, Potatoes, and Tomatoes is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crisped chicken thigh is positioned slightly off-center. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a tender interior and golden exterior, are casually arranged around the chicken, some slightly overlapping. Burst cherry tomatoes, softened and subtly charred, are scattered among the chicken and potatoes, releasing their juices onto the plate. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley adds a vibrant green accent. The overall plating is natural and inviting, reflecting a comforting home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table, with a simple, folded linen napkin placed casually nearby. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, hinting at a cozy kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, keeping the focus on the hearty, delicious food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges. Place in a large roasting pan.
Add cherry tomatoes to the pan. Smash garlic cloves and add to the pan.
Drizzle olive oil over potatoes and tomatoes. Sprinkle with oregano and thyme. Toss to coat.
Nestle chicken thighs among the vegetables in the roasting pan, skin-side up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Roasting time may vary based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Cod with Saffron Rice and Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spanish Roasted Cod with Saffron Rice and Roasted Peppers is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, roasted cod fillet, its skin golden and slightly crisp, sits prominently on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the cod, a neat mound of vibrant golden saffron rice, fluffy and studded with small red tomato pieces, adds a contrasting color and texture. Along the other side of the plate, artfully arranged strips of roasted red and yellow bell peppers, with slightly charred edges, provide bursts of color and a soft, tender texture. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes both the cod and the rice. A fresh lemon wedge rests beside the cod, ready for a squeeze. The dish features a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up juices.
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine like Albariño or Verdejo.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Halve and deseed bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skins blister and char.
Remove peppers from oven. Place in a bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap for 10 minutes. Peel skins and cut peppers into 2cm wide strips. Set aside.
Season cod fillets generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear cod fillets skin-side down for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip cod. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) and fish is opaque and flakes easily.
While cod roasts, prepare saffron rice. Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to saucepan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are coated and slightly translucent.
Pour in hot broth and steeped saffron with its water. Add diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover saucepan. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir excessively.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: Using bomba rice for the saffron rice would enhance authenticity, though medium-grain rice works well.
The saffron adds distinctive color and aroma; ensure it steeps fully before adding.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Fiery Chili-Lime Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken thighs, glistening with a fiery chili-lime glaze, is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked to a golden-brown finish, retains its whole, natural shape. Alongside the chicken are vibrant, roasted bell pepper strips in red, yellow, and orange, mixed with tender, slightly charred red onion wedges. A delicate drizzle of the reddish-orange glaze adorns the chicken and vegetables, enhancing their natural colors and adding a glossy sheen. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered thoughtfully as a garnish, adding a pop of contrasting color and freshness. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, creating a balanced and appealing composition. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: 1. Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season all sides with salt, black pepper, and chili powder.

2. Sear chicken: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet.

3. Roast vegetables: While chicken sears, preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss bell pepper strips and red onion wedges with remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender and slightly charred.
4. Prepare glaze: In a small saucepan, combine hot sauce, honey, lime juice, and minced garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened and glossy.
5. Glaze chicken: Return cooked chicken to the skillet or a bowl. Pour the chili-lime glaze over the chicken, tossing gently to coat evenly.
6. Plate dish: Arrange glazed chicken thighs on individual plates. Place roasted bell pepper strips and red onion wedges alongside. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Chicken with Paprika, Garlic, and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown, crisp-skinned roasted chicken is placed off-center on a clean white porcelain plate. Around it, rustic potato wedges, tender cherry tomato halves, and soft, caramelized garlic cloves are naturally scattered. The composition is organized yet approachable, showcasing warm colors: golden chicken, deep red tomatoes, and earthy potatoes, brightened by fresh green parsley. A generous sprinkle of chopped parsley and a bright lemon wedge garnish the dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting. This individual portion features one whole chicken piece with ample roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine or light red wine.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs or drumsticks
Small new potatoes or baby potatoes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and 10g smoked paprika.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and unpeeled garlic cloves.
Drizzle vegetables with 30ml olive oil, remaining 5g smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Toss to coat.
Add rosemary sprigs to the vegetables.
Arrange chicken pieces skin-side up on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender.
If chicken browns too quickly, loosely tent with foil.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust paprika spice level to preference (sweet vs. bittersweet).

recipes.recipe_name: German Apple-Mustard Chicken and Sausage Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of German Apple-Mustard Chicken and Sausage Bake is presented on a clean white round porcelain plate. A golden-brown, tender roasted chicken thigh sits prominently, alongside thick chunks of seared German sausage. Roasted potato wedges, caramelized onion wedges, and soft apple slices are arranged around the proteins, showcasing their varied textures and rich, earthy colors. Bright halved cherry tomatoes and vibrant yellow corn kernels are scattered throughout, adding pops of contrasting color. The dish is lightly coated in a glossy, savory-sweet mustard sauce. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the top for garnish. Beside the main dish, thin slices of gherkins are neatly placed. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and a small bowl of crusty bread nearby, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rye bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer extra whole grain or Dijon mustard on the side.
Pair with a crisp German beer or apple cider.

ingredients.name: Firm apples (e.g., Honeycrisp)
ingredients.quantity: 2, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown, about 4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add sausages. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove sausages from skillet.
Add potato wedges and onion wedges to the same skillet. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until lightly browned.
Add minced garlic and flour to skillet. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in Dijon mustard and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs and sausages to the skillet. Arrange apple wedges around them.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and corn kernels.
Return to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot with sliced gherkins and crusty bread.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, fluid risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto forms an organic, slightly mounded pool in the center, exhibiting a rich, off-white color with flecks of golden-brown seared chicken chunks, earthy sliced mushrooms, and vibrant red chili pieces. The surface glistens, indicating its creamy texture, and is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped parsley. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, showcasing the rustic searing. There is moderate negative space around the risotto on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against a soft, slightly blurred restaurant background. Traditional flatware (fork and spoon) are neatly arranged.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation. Risotto is traditionally enjoyed hot and fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same pan. Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is completely absorbed.
Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Continue adding stock and stirring until rice is creamy and al dente. It should be firm to the bite but not hard.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously (mantecatura) to create a creamy, fluid consistency.
Gently fold in the seared chicken chunks.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.
notes: Constant stirring is crucial for releasing starch from the rice and achieving a creamy risotto.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
The risotto should be loose and flowing, not stiff or dry.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Mexican Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of One-Pan Mexican Chicken and Rice is presented on a rustic, terracotta-colored ceramic plate, centered on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, browned chicken chunks nestled among fluffy, vibrant orange-red rice, plump black beans, and visible pieces of diced tomato. The rice is infused with chili and garlic. A generous layer of melted, golden-brown shredded cheddar cheese covers the top, with some bubbling edges. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is scattered over the cheese. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their rustic preparation. The plate is adequately filled but not overflowing, leaving some negative space. A small stack of warm corn tortillas rests beside the plate. A simple, unbleached cloth napkin is casually placed near the plate. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Provide a side of salsa or guacamole.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Heat oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Deseed and dice jalapeño.
Add onion, garlic, and jalapeño to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in rice and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Stir gently.
Cover skillet tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 20 minutes, or until rice is almost tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken should reach 75°C internal temperature.
Rinse and drain black beans. Stir beans into the rice mixture.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top.
Return skillet to the oven. Bake uncovered for 5-10 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Chop fresh cilantro.
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For best results, use an oven-safe skillet with a tight-fitting lid.
Adjust cayenne pepper to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Onion & Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic, ingredient-focused presentation on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The salad forms a loose, organic mound in the center, showcasing a mix of textures and natural colors. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy bread pieces are scattered throughout, providing a rustic contrast. Flaked, pale pink salmon pieces are gently integrated, visible among the grains of brown rice and translucent, pale purple pickled onion slices. Bright green chopped dill is sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh accent. A delicate drizzle of red-hued chili oil creates subtle streaks across the surface. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure beauty and simplicity of each ingredient. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Slice red onions thinly.
Combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and 5g sea salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Pour hot pickling liquid over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Cube stale rustic bread into 1.5 cm pieces.
Toss bread cubes with 20ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet.
Bake bread cubes at 180°C for 10-12 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Thinly slice fresh red chili.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a small pan over low heat. Add sliced chili. Cook gently for 5 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown. Let cool.
Season salmon fillet with salt. Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Flake salmon into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine cooked brown rice and drained pickled onions.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining 50ml olive oil with juice from half a lemon and a pinch of salt.
Add flaked salmon and crispy bread to the rice and onion mixture. Pour dressing over. Toss gently to combine.
Chop fresh dill.
Serve salad in individual bowls. Drizzle with chili oil. Garnish with chopped dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Sun-Dried Tomato Aioli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is the focal point, positioned on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a plump, golden-brown whole piece, showing a perfectly seared crust. Adjacent to the chicken, a creamy, pale orange sun-dried tomato aioli is artfully spread in a smooth, organic swirl. Beside the chicken and aioli, a vibrant pile of fresh tomato salad adds a burst of color. The salad features halved cherry tomatoes in shades of red, yellow, and orange, interspersed with translucent, thinly sliced red onion and vivid green torn basil leaves. A few scattered arugula leaves provide a subtle green base. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures and colors of each component. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlights. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Prepare sun-dried tomato aioli: Combine mayonnaise, drained sun-dried tomatoes, minced garlic, and lemon juice in a food processor. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside.

Prepare fresh tomato salad: Halve the cherry tomatoes. In a bowl, combine halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and torn basil leaves. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Gently toss to combine. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add a tablespoon of olive oil. Once hot, carefully place chicken breasts in the skillet.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and let rest for 5 minutes.
To plate, spread a generous spoonful of sun-dried tomato aioli onto one side of each plate. If using, place a small bed of arugula or mixed greens next to the aioli.
Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast on top of or beside the aioli. Spoon the fresh tomato salad alongside the chicken. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Smoked Paprika Chicken and Rice with Garlic Chili Toast
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of vibrant, reddish-orange rice forms the base, studded with diced red bell pepper and flecks of green parsley. The rice grains are distinct and glossy. Nestled atop the rice are two succulent, golden-brown chicken thighs, their skin crisp and slightly charred from searing. The chicken pieces are whole, showcasing their rich color. A light scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. Beside the main dish, on the same plate, are two golden-brown, crusty slices of garlic chili toast, showing slight char marks and bits of garlic and red chili. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the elements. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface with a neutral cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet for a rustic family-style meal.
Offer a side of simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
Accompany with a dry Spanish white wine or sangria.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and 5g smoked paprika.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic. Thinly slice red chili.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, sliced chili, remaining 10g smoked paprika, and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir well to coat rice grains with the spices and vegetables. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.

While rice cooks, prepare garlic chili toast: Slice bread into 2 cm thick pieces. In a small bowl, melt butter. Stir in a pinch of salt and a small amount of minced garlic and finely chopped red chili. Brush mixture onto bread slices.
Toast bread slices in a dry pan, under a broiler, or in a toaster oven until golden and crispy.
Once rice is cooked, remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Ensure chicken internal temperature is 75°C.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish rice with parsley. Serve immediately with garlic chili toast on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, pounded thin to about 1.5 cm thickness, is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A rich, glossy, deep amber Marsala mushroom sauce generously blankets the chicken and pools elegantly around its base. Abundant sliced cremini mushrooms are beautifully integrated within the sauce. Alongside the chicken rests a neat, creamy mound of golden-yellow polenta. The dish is vibrantly garnished with a liberal sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, adding a pop of green. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting. Served on a simple light wooden table surface, with silver cutlery and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Traditionally served with pasta (such as fettuccine or spaghetti) or creamy polenta.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to a uniform 1.5 cm thickness. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour. Shake off excess.
Heat 30ml olive oil and 30g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30g butter to skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add minced shallot and garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pan. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.

While sauce simmers, prepare polenta: Bring 750ml water or milk to a boil. Whisk in polenta slowly. Reduce heat to low. Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until creamy and thick. Season with salt.
Return chicken breasts to skillet with sauce. Simmer 1-2 minutes to heat through. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve chicken with Marsala sauce and mushrooms. Plate alongside creamy polenta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Use dry Marsala wine, not sweet dessert Marsala.
Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Onion Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cut into thick, succulent chunks, displays a deep golden-brown crust. A rich, glossy apple-onion jus, with visible softened onion slices and tender apple dice, is spooned artfully over and around the chicken, creating a natural pool of savory liquid. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered as a delicate garnish, providing a pop of green. The overall color palette is warm, featuring golden chicken, amber jus, and subtle green accents. Textures are varied: crisp chicken skin, tender meat, and soft, saucy apple and onion. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, professional yet approachable presentation in a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Apples (e.g., Gala or Honeycrisp)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cored, cut into 1 cm dice

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes until deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
Drain excess fat from skillet, leaving 15 ml. Add thinly sliced onion to skillet. Sauté over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add diced apple and grated ginger to skillet. Sauté for another 3-4 minutes until apples slightly soften.
Pour in chicken stock and apple cider vinegar. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid slightly thickens and flavors meld.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season jus with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested chicken thighs into 2-3 thick chunks each.
Plate chicken chunks. Spoon apple-onion jus generously over and around chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Crusted Pork Loin with Chili Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A refined main course on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The centerpiece is a generous portion of roasted pork loin, presented as thick, golden-crusted chunks. The pork boasts a crisp, textured mustard-breadcrumb crust with visible rosemary, contrasting with the tender interior. Beside the pork, a cluster of golden-brown chili-roasted potato wedges shows a crisp exterior and hints of red chili flakes. A rich, glossy mound of deeply caramelized onion confit, amber in color, complements the other elements. Plating is balanced, with moderate negative space. Colors are natural: golden-browns, rich amber, and subtle green from the rosemary garnish. A modern bistro setting features a simple wooden table, standard European flatware, and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove pork from pan. Set aside.
In a small bowl, combine Dijon mustard, panko breadcrumbs, and finely chopped fresh rosemary. Mix well to form a thick paste.
Spread the mustard mixture evenly over the seared pork loin, coating all sides.

Place pork loin back into the hot pan. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) for medium, or 70°C (160°F) for well-done. Remove from oven, transfer to a cutting board, tent with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.

While pork roasts, prepare potatoes. Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with remaining 30 ml olive oil, red chili flakes, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven as pork for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.

Prepare onion confit. Thinly slice onions. Melt butter in a separate pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut rested pork loin into thick, un-fanned chunks. Arrange pork chunks on plates with chili-roasted potato wedges and onion confit. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig, if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Allow the pork to rest fully before cutting to ensure juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Fermented Tomato & Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A single, beautifully plated portion of braised chicken on a handcrafted, natural ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A whole, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests at the center. Beside it, a rich, deep red sauce of tender, whole fermented cherry tomatoes and wilted dark green seasonal greens pools naturally. Roasted potato chunks, with their rustic, golden-brown skins and fluffy interiors, are casually arranged next to the chicken. A few fresh rosemary leaves are scattered over the potatoes. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting, emphasizing the dish's organic and sustainable essence.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Dice onion into small cubes. Mince garlic. Add onion to the pan, sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and 1 rosemary sprig. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in fermented cherry tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover the pan.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30 minutes.
While chicken braises, scrub potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm chunks. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper, and remaining rosemary sprigs.
Spread potatoes on a baking tray. Roast in the same oven as chicken for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
Check chicken internal temperature; it should be 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Stir in seasonal greens into the braising liquid. Cook until just wilted. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve one braised chicken thigh per plate. Spoon generous amount of fermented tomato sauce and wilted greens alongside. Arrange roasted potato chunks next to chicken.
notes: To minimize waste, use chicken bones and vegetable scraps to make homemade chicken stock for this recipe. Potato peels can be crisped for a snack or added to stock.
Any leftover braising liquid can be frozen for future use as a flavorful sauce base.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna with Cauliflower Carrot Puree and Verjus Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single serving on a clean white porcelain plate. A smooth, vibrant orange-gold cauliflower carrot puree forms the base. Resting atop is a thick, seared tuna steak, 2.5 cm, with a deep golden-brown crust and a rosy-pink medium-rare interior. A creamy, pale yellow verjus mustard sauce artfully encircles the tuna and puree. Finely chopped fresh green parsley garnishes the composition, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware accompany the dish. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors, creating an inviting bistro aesthetic.
instructions: For the Cauliflower Carrot Puree:
Peel carrots. Cut carrots and cauliflower into 2 cm florets/chunks.
Mince garlic.
In a pot, combine carrots, cauliflower, garlic, and enough water or broth to just cover. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain vegetables, reserving some cooking liquid.
Transfer vegetables and garlic to a blender. Add butter.
Blend until smooth. Add reserved liquid gradually for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the Verjus Mustard Sauce:
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and verjus.
Slowly drizzle in 60ml olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified.
Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
For the Seared Tuna:
Pat tuna steaks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Add a drizzle of olive oil.
Sear tuna steaks for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare (internal temperature 50-55°C), or longer for desired doneness.
Remove tuna from pan. Let rest 2 minutes before serving.
Assembly:
Spoon a generous portion of cauliflower carrot puree onto the center of each plate.
Place one seared tuna steak on top of the puree.
Spoon verjus mustard sauce around the tuna and puree.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Braised Chicken with Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Homestyle Braised Chicken with Onions rests on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, centered on a well-used wooden kitchen table. One plump, golden-brown bone-in chicken thigh, its skin richly caramelized, is nestled amongst tender, thick-cut onion wedges that have softened and taken on a deep, translucent amber hue from the braising liquid. A rich, savory sauce, glistening with pan juices and infused with herbs, pools around the chicken and onions. The dish is presented with a rustic fork and knife, a casually folded plain linen napkin to the side. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the food. The background is simple, suggesting a lived-in family dining area. No fanned meat slices are present; the chicken is served whole.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in plain flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5 minutes. Flip and sear the other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add thick-cut onion wedges to the pot. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Cook until the wine has reduced by half.
Pour in chicken broth. Add fresh thyme and rosemary sprigs. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
Return the seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure the liquid mostly covers the chicken, but the skin remains exposed above the liquid.
Cover the pot with a lid. Transfer the pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 40-50 minutes, or until the chicken's internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Carefully remove the pot from the oven. Let the chicken rest in the pot for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This recipe focuses on simple techniques for a comforting, hearty meal.
Chicken thighs are ideal for braising as they remain tender and flavorful.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Cucumber and White Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, sustainable salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. The base features a bed of crisp, mixed salad greens. Arranged artfully on top are thinly sliced, translucent pickled cucumber rounds, contrasting with vibrant red diced tomatoes and creamy white beans. Delicate, ruby-red radish slices add pops of color. Small, flaky pieces of drained tuna are scattered sparingly amongst the vegetables. A light, clear vinaigrette, made with pickling liquid and olive oil, glistens on the ingredients. Fresh green dill sprigs are scattered for garnish. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The overall impression is fresh, clean, and inviting, emphasizing the natural beauty and textures of the seasonal ingredients under soft natural lighting, with a minimalist background suggesting natural elements.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in water or oil

instructions: Prepare pickled cucumbers: In a non-reactive bowl, combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Stir until dissolved. Add cucumber slices. Let marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare remaining ingredients: Dice tomatoes. Rinse and drain white beans. Thinly slice radishes.
Make the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 30 ml of the cucumber pickling liquid, olive oil, and half of the chopped dill. Season with black pepper.
Assemble the salad: In a large bowl, combine drained pickled cucumber slices, diced tomatoes, white beans, sliced radishes, and mixed salad greens.
Add tuna: Gently flake the tuna and add to the salad.
Dress and serve: Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Garnish with remaining fresh dill. Serve immediately.
Recipe serves 4 people.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Pork Chili
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of thick, hearty chili is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The chili, a rich reddish-brown, is chunky with visible ground beef and pork, dark kidney beans, and softened diced red bell pepper. A dollop of cool, white sour cream melts slowly on top, partially covered by a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh cilantro. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl, along with a sturdy, silver spoon. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread or a side of tortilla chips.
Offer extra shredded cheddar cheese and chopped green onions for topping.
recipes.hero_ingredient: Hearty Chili with Ground Meats and Beans

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef and ground pork. Cook, breaking up meat with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced red bell pepper to the pot. Cook until vegetables soften, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add drained kidney beans.
Bring chili to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Smoked Paprika Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate, embodying natural simplicity. A base of vibrant mixed salad greens holds glossy, ruby-red fermented cherry tomato halves, their natural shapes highlighted. Uniformly diced cucumber cubes add a cool green, while thinly sliced red onion provides a subtle purple. Small, 0.5 cm cubed Gouda cheese pieces are scattered, offering creamy yellow accents. Thinly sliced, rehydrated dark red chili rings provide a pop of color and texture. The ingredients are lightly coated with a glistening, orange-hued smoked paprika dressing, ensuring all components are visible and artfully distributed. Fresh basil leaves serve as a natural garnish. The composition maintains ample negative space, emphasizing each ingredient's beauty. The setting features a light reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting, creating an eco-conscious, minimalist aesthetic.
instructions: Wash and halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a clean glass jar. Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to make a 3% brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plate to keep tomatoes under brine. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily if not using an airlock. Once fermented, store in refrigerator.
Rehydrate dried chili pod in warm water for 20 minutes until softened. Remove stem and seeds. Thinly slice the rehydrated chili into rings or small strips.
Wash mixed salad greens. Pat dry. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion into half-moons.
Cut Gouda cheese into small 0.5 cm cubes or crumble it.
In a small bowl, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, diced cucumber, and sliced red onion. Add the fermented cherry tomatoes (drain brine before adding).

Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat. Arrange salad on individual plates. Scatter the sliced rehydrated chili and Gouda cubes over the top. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for tomatoes based on desired tartness and ambient temperature.
The brine from fermented tomatoes can be repurposed as a flavorful dressing component or soup base.
Leftover vegetable scraps can be used for homemade vegetable broth, promoting zero-waste cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Vegetables is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned bone-in chicken thigh is the central element. Rustic potato wedges, large chunks of roasted red onion, vibrant whole roasted cherry tomatoes, and scattered tender chickpeas surround the chicken. The vegetables show slight caramelization and varied textures. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for moderate negative space, showcasing the dish's balanced composition. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the food. Standard silver flatware is arranged beside the plate. A slice of crusty bread rests on the side, ready for dipping. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Offer a side of simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Red onion, cut into large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, oregano, and smoked paprika.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, onion chunks, cherry tomatoes, chickpeas, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Potato Rösti and Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate centered on a simple wooden table. A perfectly golden-brown, crisp-edged potato rösti, formed into a neat disc, rests to one side. Beside it, a whole, plump pan-seared chicken breast, displaying a beautiful golden-brown crust from searing, sits prominently. A rich, velvety mushroom cream sauce is artfully spooned over the chicken, cascading slightly onto the plate, adding a luxurious sheen. The sauce is speckled with tender, sliced cremini mushrooms. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced, professional, and inviting. The setting is a modern bistro, with a cotton napkin placed beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

For the Potato Rösti: Peel and coarsely grate potatoes. Rinse grated potatoes under cold water until water runs clear. Squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly using a clean kitchen towel. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 20g butter in a large non-stick oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add half of the grated potatoes, pressing down firmly to form a flat, even layer. Cook for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy on the bottom. Carefully flip the rösti and cook for another 5-7 minutes until the second side is golden. Repeat for the second rösti or cook simultaneously in two pans. Keep warm in the oven.
For the Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 10g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

For the Mushroom Cream Sauce: While chicken bakes, add remaining 10g butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same skillet (or a clean one) over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms and thyme sprigs. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.

Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half again. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Remove thyme sprigs. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.

To Serve: Place a potato rösti on each plate. Arrange one pan-seared chicken breast beside the rösti. Spoon mushroom cream sauce generously over the chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure potatoes are very dry before cooking for crispy rösti.
Resting the chicken ensures it remains juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Squash & Corn Crémeux with Candied Chicken Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A refined dessert presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A single elegant quenelle of the creamy, pale orange-yellow Roasted Squash & Corn Crémeux is centered. A vibrant, smooth orange Roasted Carrot Sauce is artfully swiped or pooled beside the crémeux. One or two delicate, translucent, deep amber caramelized onion tuiles are strategically placed, adding verticality and crisp texture. A small, precise sprinkle of golden-brown candied chicken crisps, about 0.5 cm in size, provides a contrasting textural element and a hint of unexpected flavor. A tiny, fresh green mint sprig serves as a final garnish, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and professional, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the smooth textures of the crémeux and sauce, and the crispness of the tuiles and chicken. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, complementing the modern bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Place squash and corn kernels on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and caramelized. Let cool slightly. Puree roasted squash and corn until smooth.

For the Crémeux: In a medium saucepan, heat heavy cream over medium heat until simmering. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, 50 g sugar, and vanilla extract until pale. Slowly temper hot cream into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (80-82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in squash-corn puree and a pinch of salt. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until firm.

For the Onion Tuiles: Thinly slice the yellow onion. In a small non-stick pan, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion and 25 g sugar. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Spread caramelized onion very thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 150°C for 15-20 minutes, until crisp. Break into irregular pieces.

For the Candied Chicken Crisps: Dice chicken breast into 0.5 cm cubes. Heat a small non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook, stirring, until golden brown and crisp (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. In the same pan, combine remaining 25 g sugar and 30 ml water. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook until syrup slightly thickens. Add crispy chicken back to the pan. Stir quickly to coat chicken in the glaze. Spread chicken onto parchment paper to cool and harden.

For the Carrot Sauce: Cut carrots into 1 cm rounds. Place in a small pot with orange juice, honey, and a pinch of salt. Add enough water to barely cover. Bring to a simmer. Cook until carrots are very tender. Drain most liquid, reserving a small amount. Puree carrots with reserved liquid until very smooth. Adjust consistency with more water if needed. Season to taste.

To Plate: Spoon a quenelle or scoop of the chilled crémeux onto one side of a clean white round plate. Swipe a generous spoonful of carrot sauce across the plate beside the crémeux. Arrange 1-2 caramelized onion tuile pieces standing upright next to the crémeux. Sprinkle a small amount of candied chicken crisps around the crémeux. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
The candied chicken crisps provide a unique sweet-savory crunch. Use sparingly as a textural garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Zharkoye
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Chicken and Potato Zharkoye is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, set on a well-used wooden dining table. Large, tender chunks of braised chicken, golden-brown from searing, are nestled among hearty potato wedges, vibrant red and green bell pepper pieces, and earthy mushrooms. The rich, savory tomato-based broth coats all ingredients, with steam gently rising. A generous dollop of thick, white smetana (sour cream) rests on one side, and a few sprigs of fresh, bright green dill are scattered over the top. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl. A slice of dark rye bread is casually placed nearby on the table. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the homely, hearty dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of smetana (sour cream) on the side.
Accompany with slices of dark rye bread.
Offer a side of pickled cucumbers or tomatoes for a traditional touch.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, bell peppers cut into large dice, and halved or quartered mushrooms to the pot. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, bay leaves, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C / 167°F). Potatoes should be tender.
Remove bay leaves. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot.
notes: This hearty stew is a classic Russian comfort food, perfect for a family meal.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented in a shallow, matte off-white ceramic bowl, centered on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The risotto, a pale, earthy beige, forms a natural, slightly mounded pool. Scattered atop the risotto are tender, pulled chicken pieces, retaining their natural irregular shapes and golden-brown seared edges. Crisp, golden chicken skin shards are artfully placed for textural contrast. Alongside, a vibrant small mound of finely diced, multi-colored fermented vegetable relish (orange carrots, purple radish, pale green cabbage) adds a pop of color and freshness. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing ample negative space. Natural light bathes the scene, highlighting the textures. A simple, undyed linen napkin rests subtly to the side. No overcrowding; the dish is the focal point, celebrating ingredient purity and sustainable ethos.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps (carrot, celery, leek greens, onion skins)
Mixed Seasonal Vegetables (for relish, e.g., carrot, radish, cabbage)

instructions: Debone chicken. Reserve bones and carcass for broth. Separate skin. Cut meat into large chunks.
Place bones, carcass, vegetable scraps, bay leaf, and peppercorns in a large pot. Add 2.5 litres cold water.
Bring to a simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 2 hours.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Keep broth warm.
Season chicken meat chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken in a pan with 15 ml olive oil until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C. Remove chicken.
Render chicken skin in the same pan over medium heat until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towel. Crumble into shards.
For the fermented relish: Wash and finely dice or julienne mixed seasonal vegetables.
Dissolve 5 g sea salt in 250 ml filtered water to make a brine.
Place vegetables in a clean jar. Pour brine over, ensuring vegetables are submerged.
Seal jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.
For the risotto: In a large pot, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter. Sauté diced onion until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Toast 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until completely absorbed.
Add warm chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to absorb before adding more.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, until rice is al dente and creamy.
Stir in remaining 40 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Fold in seared chicken chunks.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls.
Top each serving with crumbled crispy chicken skin shards.
Spoon a small portion of fermented vegetable relish alongside or on top of the risotto.
notes: The fermented vegetable relish can be prepared in advance. Adjust vegetables based on seasonal availability.

recipes.recipe_name: Brined Chicken with Fermented Potato Salad and Root Green Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted brined chicken is artfully presented on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, resting on a light bamboo table. The bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, cooked to a deep golden-brown with crispy skin, is placed whole, not sliced. Adjacent to it is a generous, organic mound of creamy potato salad, featuring tender, medium-cubed potatoes interspersed with vibrant, finely diced quick-pickled red onions and fresh green herbs. A bright, verdant root green pesto is artfully drizzled over the chicken and potato salad, adding a burst of color and flavor. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, allowing natural textures and colors of each ingredient to shine. An undyed linen napkin and a simple, unadorned fork complement the eco-conscious aesthetic. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, sustainable appeal.

ingredients.name: Waxy potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold, new potatoes)
Fermented pickle brine (from sauerkraut or dill pickles) OR fermented hot sauce
ingredients.quantity: 30 mL brine OR 5 mL hot sauce

ingredients.name: Mixed root greens (e.g., carrot tops, radish greens, beet greens)

instructions: Prepare Chicken Brine: Combine 1 L water, 60 g salt, 30 g sugar, 2 bay leaves, 10 black peppercorns in a pot. Bring to a boil, stir to dissolve salt and sugar. Remove from heat. Cool completely.
Brine Chicken: Submerge chicken thighs in cooled brine. Refrigerate for 4-6 hours. Remove chicken, pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.

Roast Chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C. Drizzle chicken with 15 mL olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Place on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is crispy. Rest 5 minutes.
Cook Potatoes: Wash 600 g waxy potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until tender. Drain well. Cool completely.
Quick-Pickle Red Onion: Thinly slice 1/2 red onion, then finely dice. In a small bowl, combine diced red onion with 60 mL white wine vinegar and 5 g sugar. Let sit for 15 minutes. Drain liquid.
Assemble Potato Salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled potato cubes, drained pickled red onion, 30 g chopped fresh dill, 30 g chopped fresh parsley, and 15 g chopped fresh chives.

Make Potato Salad Dressing: Whisk 60 mL olive oil, 30 mL fermented pickle brine (or 5 mL fermented hot sauce), 15 mL lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Pour dressing over potato mixture. Gently toss to combine.

Prepare Root Green Pesto: Wash 100 g mixed root greens. Blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water to shock. Squeeze greens dry. In a food processor, combine blanched greens, 50 g walnuts/sunflower seeds, 2 peeled garlic cloves, 30 mL lemon juice, 5 g nutritional yeast (if using), salt, and pepper. Pulse until coarsely chopped. Slowly drizzle in 100 mL olive oil while processing until smooth but still textured. Adjust consistency with a splash of potato cooking water if needed.
Plate Dish: Place a roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange a generous mound of potato salad next to the chicken. Drizzle root green pesto over both chicken and potato salad. Serve immediately.
notes: Zero-waste tip: Reserve chicken bones for making stock. Any vegetable trimmings can also be used for stock. Potato cooking water can be used to thin the pesto or as a base for vegetable stock.
This recipe emphasizes plant-forward components through the substantial potato salad and the vibrant root green pesto, complementing the sustainably prepared chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tuscan Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic red-orange tomato sauce, infused with oregano and garlic. Tender, seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled amidst the pasta and sauce. Diced red bell peppers and onions are visible within the sauce, adding vibrant color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped oregano leaves garnishes the dish, providing a contrasting green. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point with a soft, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped oregano or basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Rice Salad with Smoked Paprika Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper & Rice Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, typical of a Spanish home kitchen. Diced roasted bell peppers (red, yellow, orange) are mixed with cooled short-grain rice. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes, diced green cucumber, and finely diced red onion add vibrant color and varied textures. Fresh green chopped parsley is generously mixed throughout. A glossy, reddish-orange smoked paprika vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients, creating a satisfying, unpretentious mound. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. Simple ceramic plates and basic flatware are casually placed. A rustic linen napkin is loosely draped. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family dining area with minimal, natural clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced bell peppers with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, roasted bell peppers, halved cherry tomatoes, finely diced red onion, and diced cucumber.
For the dressing, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, smoked paprika, dried chili flakes, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately or chill for later.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Tomato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic chicken and tomato soup is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. The soup is a rich, warm red from the crushed tomatoes, with visible, tender chunks of diced chicken (2cm cubes). Soft, small diced vegetables like carrots, celery, and onion (1cm cubes) are dispersed throughout, adding subtle color and texture. A thin swirl of golden olive oil glistens on the surface. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are casually placed on top, adding a pop of color. The bowl is surrounded by a simple, casually folded linen napkin and a sturdy wooden spoon, emphasizing a comfortable, homely kitchen setting. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting steam rising from the soup. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen, with minimal, unobtrusive elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Offer a side of grated Parmesan cheese
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook, stirring, until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add dried oregano, dried basil, and bay leaf.
Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve with optional grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: This recipe focuses on simple, comforting flavors perfect for home cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Fish Tacos with Chili-Lime Crema
recipes.visual_description: Three vibrant Crispy Fish Tacos are arranged artfully on a clean white porcelain plate, slightly overlapping. Each warm corn tortilla cradles golden-brown, irregularly shaped chunks of crispy fried white fish, showing their crunchy texture. A generous mound of thinly shredded green cabbage slaw, flecked with bright red onion and fresh cilantro, sits atop the fish, providing a fresh contrast. A creamy, pale orange Chili-Lime Crema is drizzled liberally over the slaw, forming delicate ribbons. Scattered fresh cilantro leaves add a final touch of verdant green. A quartered lime wedge rests beside the tacos, ready for squeezing. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional lime wedges for squeezing.
Offer a side of authentic Mexican salsa (e.g., salsa roja or salsa verde).
Provide pickled red onions as an optional topping.
instructions: Prepare the Chili-Lime Crema: In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, lime juice, chipotle chili powder, garlic powder, and salt. Refrigerate until serving.
Prepare the Cabbage Slaw: In a medium bowl, combine shredded green cabbage, sliced red onion, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle with lime juice and olive oil. Season with salt. Toss to combine.
Prepare the Fish Batter: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Gradually whisk in cold sparkling water until a smooth, thin batter forms. Do not overmix.

Fry the Fish: Heat vegetable oil in a large deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C. Cut fish into 3 cm wide strips. Dip each fish strip into the batter, ensuring it is fully coated. Carefully place battered fish strips into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot. Fry for 3-4 minutes per batch, or until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drain the Fish: Remove fried fish with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

Warm the Tortillas: Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Warm tortillas for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable and slightly charred. Stack and wrap in a clean kitchen towel to keep warm.

Assemble Tacos: Place 2-3 fish strips in each warm tortilla. Top with a generous spoonful of cabbage slaw. Drizzle with Chili-Lime Crema. Garnish with extra cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: For best results, use very cold sparkling water for the batter to ensure crispiness.
Do not overcrowd the frying pot to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Buckwheat Kasha and Dill Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, its skin golden-brown and crisped, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is nestled atop a generous, slightly mounded portion of fluffy, earthy brown buckwheat kasha, its individual grains distinct. Adjacent to the kasha, a vibrant green mound of diced cucumber salad is presented, liberally flecked with fresh green dill and coated in a creamy white dressing. The composition features contrasting textures: the crispy chicken skin, tender chicken meat, and firm, distinct buckwheat grains, balanced by the crisp cucumber and creamy salad. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the food, with a subtle, blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with pickled vegetables.
Can be accompanied by a traditional fermented beverage like kvass.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on a baking tray. Roast for 35-40 minutes, until skin is golden and crispy. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
While chicken roasts, rinse buckwheat groats thoroughly under cold water. Drain well.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed buckwheat groats to the saucepan. Toast lightly for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and buckwheat is tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Dice cucumber into small cubes. Chop fresh dill.
In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, chopped dill, sour cream, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Mix well.
To serve, place a portion of buckwheat kasha on each plate. Top with one roasted chicken thigh. Place a scoop of dill cucumber salad alongside.
notes: Chicken roasting time may vary based on thigh size. Use a meat thermometer to ensure safety.
Buckwheat kasha can be prepared in advance and reheated gently.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Garlic Herb Chicken and Cheesy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Skillet Garlic Herb Chicken and Cheesy Potatoes is casually arranged on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a simple rim. Thick chunks of golden-brown, seared chicken are nestled among rustic wedges of roasted potatoes. The chicken and potatoes are coated with melted, gooey Cheddar cheese, which drapes over some pieces. The surface of the dish shows a mix of textures: the tender, slightly crispy exterior of the chicken, the soft interior and browned skin of the potatoes, and the luscious, bubbling cheese. A sprinkle of vibrant green, chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the top, adding a touch of freshness. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing its natural grain. A casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is lit with warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, focusing all attention on the hearty, comforting dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut chicken thighs into thick chunks. Cut potatoes into rustic wedges.
Mince garlic. Chop fresh parsley.
Toss potato wedges with 15 ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, pepper, oregano, and thyme. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Carefully add roasted potato wedges to the skillet with the garlic. Stir gently to combine.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet with the potatoes. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese evenly over the chicken and potatoes. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
