Add ginger and chilies: Stir in grated ginger and slit green chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add spices: Reduce heat slightly. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Stir constantly for 30 seconds until aromatic, being careful not to burn.

Build curry: Add cooked chickpeas, vegetable broth, and tamarind paste to the pot. Stir well to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and liquid to slightly reduce.
Finish curry: Stir in the full-fat coconut milk. Simmer gently for another 5 minutes. Do not boil vigorously after adding coconut milk. Season with salt to taste.
Serve: Ladle the Zero-Waste Coconut & Tamarind Chickpea Curry into individual bowls. Top each serving with a portion of the quick-pickled radishes and a generous sprinkle of the carrot top gremolata.
notes: This recipe emphasizes plant-forward, zero-waste cooking. Vegetable broth can be made from saved kitchen scraps (onion skins, carrot peels, herb stems).
The 'fermented' aspect is primarily achieved through the quick-pickled radishes, adding a tangy, preserved element to the meal.
traditional_techniques: Use of fresh curry leaves and coconut milk for flavor depth

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Sesame Bok Choy
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Miso-Glazed Salmon is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pan-seared salmon fillet, with its crisped, golden-brown skin and caramelized, rich amber glaze, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Its flaky texture is visible where the glaze adheres. Alongside the salmon, vibrant green bok choy halves, lightly charred from searing, are neatly arranged, showcasing their tender-crisp structure. The dish is garnished with a scattering of toasted white sesame seeds over the salmon and bok choy, adding a subtle crunch and nutty aroma. Thinly sliced bright green onions are sprinkled atop the salmon, providing a fresh color contrast. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A set of elegant dark wood chopsticks lies beside the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin is folded nearby. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed short-grain rice.
Offer a small dish of pickled ginger as an accompaniment.
instructions: Combine miso paste, mirin, sake, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, minced garlic, and grated ginger in a bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Place salmon fillets in a shallow dish. Pour half of the miso glaze over salmon. Ensure fillets are coated. Marinate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Heat vegetable oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear salmon, skin-side down, for 3-4 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Brush generously with remaining miso glaze. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until salmon reaches desired doneness and flakes easily.
While salmon bakes, heat a separate pan with a splash of oil. Add bok choy, cut-side down. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly charred. Flip and cook for another 2 minutes until tender-crisp.
Remove salmon from oven. Let rest for 2 minutes.

Plate each salmon fillet on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange two bok choy halves beside the salmon. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Garlic Stuffed Acorn Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single acorn squash half, golden-orange and tender from roasting, is centrally placed on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate. The squash is generously filled with a creamy, savory mixture of cottage cheese, finely minced garlic, and herbs, topped with a thick layer of melted mozzarella cheese that has bubbled and turned a rich golden-brown in places. The filling is slightly mounded, showcasing its hearty volume. Flecks of fresh green parsley garnish the top, adding a pop of color. The plate is set on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A casual folded cloth napkin and standard metal fork rest beside the plate, completing the homely, inviting scene. Portions are modest and comforting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash acorn squash. Carefully cut each squash in half lengthwise. Scoop out and discard seeds and fibrous bits.
Lightly brush the cut sides of the squash with 15 ml olive oil. Season with 2.5 g salt and 1 g black pepper.
Place squash halves cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 30 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork.
While squash roasts, prepare the filling. Mince garlic cloves finely.
In a medium bowl, combine cottage cheese, 100 g shredded mozzarella, minced garlic, dried oregano, remaining 2.5 g salt, and 1 g black pepper. Mix well.
Once squash is tender, remove from oven. Carefully flip the squash halves so they are cut-side up.
Spoon the cottage cheese mixture evenly into each squash cavity. Mound the filling slightly.
Top each stuffed squash half with the remaining 50 g shredded mozzarella.
Return to oven. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden brown.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Coffee-Chipotle Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single serving of two richly browned chicken thighs, nestled in a deep, glossy, reddish-brown coffee-chipotle sauce. The chicken, cooked to tender perfection, retains its whole, un-sliced form, showcasing its crispy, seared skin. The sauce, thick and aromatic, pools around the chicken, its surface shimmering slightly. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro leaves provides a contrasting green against the dark sauce and chicken. The meal is served on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple wooden table. Beside the plate, a small stack of warm, pliable corn tortillas are neatly arranged, ready for scooping the savory sauce and chicken. The setting is minimalist with natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point within a casual bistro atmosphere. No distracting elements are present, ensuring the focus remains on the authentic Mexican presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Steamed white rice
Pickled red onions
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, oregano, and cocoa powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in brewed coffee, chipotle hot sauce, crushed tomatoes, and chicken broth. Stir well, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot, nestling it into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and is tender.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken with sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with warm corn tortillas.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chipotle hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Chocolate Red Wine Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The short ribs, a rich, dark mahogany brown, appear incredibly tender and succulent, with some natural marbling visible. They are nestled on a creamy, pale yellow bed of soft polenta. A generous, glossy pool of the dark reddish-brown chocolate red wine sauce envelops the ribs and gently merges with the polenta base. The sauce glistens under soft, natural light, highlighting its rich texture. A vibrant green gremolata, made from finely chopped parsley, bright lemon zest, and minced garlic, is lightly sprinkled over the top of the short ribs, providing a fresh color contrast. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a relaxed modern bistro atmosphere with even, natural lighting. The composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing the dish as the clear focal point.
instructions: Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches if needed. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 5 minutes, reducing wine by half.
Return short ribs to the Dutch oven. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the Dutch oven.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until ribs are fork-tender.
Carefully remove ribs from the Dutch oven. Tent with foil to keep warm.
Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Bring sauce to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in finely chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
To make gremolata, combine chopped parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Serve short ribs with the chocolate red wine sauce. Garnish with gremolata.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Enchiladas Rojas
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-baked chicken and potato enchiladas, generously coated in a vibrant, glossy red chile sauce, are arranged neatly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, ruby-red sauce envelops the rolled corn tortillas, revealing glimpses of the savory shredded chicken and creamy potato filling. A blanket of bubbling, melted Monterey Jack cheese crowns the enchiladas, boasting a delicate golden-brown crust. A delicate drizzle of cool Mexican crema artfully zigzags across the cheese, complemented by a scattering of crumbled white queso fresco, vibrant green cilantro leaves, and finely diced crimson red onion. The presentation is balanced, with ample negative space. A cotton napkin and traditional flatware rest beside the plate on a simple wooden surface, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Mexican rice and refried beans.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Accompaniments like pico de gallo or pickled jalapeños are common.
instructions: Boil chicken breast or thigh in salted water until cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, cool, then shred finely. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Boil until tender. Drain well. Combine with shredded chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Mash lightly or leave some potato chunks for texture.

For the sauce, remove stems and seeds from dried Ancho and Guajillo chiles. Toast chiles lightly in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side. Place chiles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
While chiles rehydrate, halve and toast Roma tomatoes, half an onion, and garlic cloves in a dry pan until lightly charred. Do not burn.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Blend chiles, toasted tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 250 ml chicken broth, cumin, and oregano until very smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids.

Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. Pour in the strained chile sauce. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and deepens in color. Season with salt to taste. Add more broth if sauce is too thick.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Heat remaining 30 ml vegetable oil in a shallow pan over medium heat. Briefly dip each corn tortilla in the hot oil for 10-15 seconds per side to soften. Do not crisp. Drain on paper towels.

Dip each softened tortilla into the chile sauce, coating both sides. Fill each tortilla with approximately 60 grams of the chicken and potato mixture. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the prepared baking dish.
Pour any remaining chile sauce over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle generously with shredded Monterey Jack cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the enchiladas are heated through.
Serve immediately. Garnish each serving with a drizzle of Mexican crema, crumbled queso fresco, fresh chopped cilantro, and finely diced red onion.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The quality of dried chiles significantly impacts the sauce flavor.
traditional_techniques: Soften tortillas in oil for rolling

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz Picante con Pimientos Asados
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous single portion of vibrant orange-red rice forms the centerpiece, its color derived from paprika and tomato. The rice is fluffy yet moist, studded with tender, slightly charred strips of roasted red bell pepper and flecks of finely sliced red chili, offering visual contrast and a hint of heat. Finely minced garlic and diced onion are integrated seamlessly within the grains. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a single fork and a small side of crusty bread, evoking a casual Spanish dining experience under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in any remaining pan juices.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness of the rice.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast whole red bell peppers for 25-30 minutes until skin is blistered and charred. Transfer to a bowl, cover tightly, and let steam for 10 minutes. Peel, remove seeds, and cut roasted peppers into thick strips. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, finely sliced fresh red chili, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat rice grains with the aromatic mixture. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken stock. Stir once to distribute ingredients. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Remove from heat. Gently fold in the roasted red pepper strips. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Mushroom Torte with Orange Curd
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous wedge of rich, dark chocolate torte is positioned cleanly on a round, white porcelain plate. The torte features a dense, moist crumb with a deep, glossy brown color. Alongside the torte, a vibrant, golden-orange curd is elegantly spooned, its smooth, luscious texture contrasting with the torte's solidity. Scattered across the plate and atop the curd are crisp, golden-brown toasted coconut flakes, adding a delicate crunch and visual warmth. The presentation is simple yet refined, highlighting the contrasting colors and textures. The plate rests on a clean, light-colored wooden table surface, illuminated by soft, natural light, creating a professional and approachable bistro aesthetic. A plain white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The entire plate and its contents are visible, with ample negative space around the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Melt dark chocolate and 150 g butter together in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk 3 large eggs with brown sugar until light and fluffy. Stir in the zest of one orange.
Fold the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture until combined.
Sift together flour, cocoa powder, porcini mushroom powder, and salt. Gently fold into the chocolate batter until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out with moist crumbs. Do not overbake. Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack.
For the orange curd: In a medium saucepan, whisk together juice of two oranges (about 100 ml), zest of one orange, 2 large eggs, and granulated sugar.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil.

Remove from heat. Whisk in 60 g cold butter, cubed, until fully melted and smooth. Strain the curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming. Chill until firm.
To serve: Slice the cooled torte into 4 portions. Plate each slice. Spoon a dollop of chilled orange curd alongside. Sprinkle with toasted coconut flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Creamy Mushroom Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallions rests centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, golden-brown beef medallions, approximately 2.5 cm thick, are positioned slightly overlapping. A rich, creamy, light brown mushroom-mustard sauce is generously spooned over and around the beef, pooling elegantly on the plate. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms are visible within the sauce. Alongside the beef, vibrant roasted bell pepper strips, a mix of red and yellow, are neatly arranged, showcasing their tender texture and slightly charred edges. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley over the beef and sauce, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is professional yet inviting, with balanced negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut beef tenderloin into 4 medallions. Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut red and yellow bell peppers into thick strips. Toss bell pepper strips with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes until tender and slightly charred.
Slice cremini mushrooms. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate. Tent with foil.
Add 15 grams butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until golden brown.
Add diced shallots to the skillet. Cook 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Whisk in heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Return beef medallions to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over beef.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with roasted bell peppers.
notes: Resting the beef after searing is crucial for juiciness.
Adjust mustard quantity to your preference for a stronger or milder flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pea & Liver Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden-amber consommé is presented in a minimalist, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, off-white finish. The soup features tender, light brown beef liver chunks (2cm cubes) nestled amongst vibrant green fermented peas and soft white potato cubes. A scattering of bright green, finely sliced celery crescents and delicate celery leaves floats on the surface, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is clean and unfussy, with ample negative space around the ingredients within the bowl, allowing their natural colors and textures to stand out. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually placed beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the transparency of the broth and the organic beauty of the ingredients. The background is simple and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Rinse dried peas. Soak peas in water for 12 hours. Drain.

Place soaked peas in a clean jar. Prepare a brine by dissolving 2g of salt for every 100ml of non-chlorinated water. Cover peas completely with this brine. Ensure peas are submerged. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock.
Ferment peas at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days until slightly tangy and fizzy. Refrigerate to halt fermentation.
Cut beef liver into 2cm cubes. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Dice onion, carrot, and half of the celery into 1cm pieces. Reserve celery leaves and remaining celery stalk for garnish and stock.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear liver cubes quickly until browned on all sides, about 2 minutes. Do not cook through. Remove liver and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and seared liver to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam that rises to the surface. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Do not boil.
Carefully strain the consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids.
Peel potatoes. Cut 200g of potato into 1cm cubes. Cut remaining 100g of potato into small dice (0.5cm) for garnish.
Add potato cubes (200g) to the strained consommé. Simmer until tender, about 10-12 minutes.
Add 100g of the fermented peas and the small diced potato (100g) during the last 3 minutes of cooking to heat through.
Stir in verjus. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely slice reserved celery stalk into thin crescents. Chop reserved celery leaves for garnish.
Ladle consommé into bowls. Garnish with sliced celery and celery leaves.
notes: For zero-waste, vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends) can be used to make a dedicated vegetable stock or to fortify the chicken stock.
The fermented peas add a unique tangy depth and probiotic benefits.
Verjus offers a subtle acidity without the harshness of vinegar, aligning with a minimalistic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tomato Artichoke Pasta Soup with Herbed Cottage Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic soup bowl holds a single individual portion of the hearty soup. The rich, reddish-orange tomato broth is filled with visible pieces of small ditalini pasta, softened diced onion, and tender quartered artichoke hearts. A creamy white dollop of cottage cheese, lightly swirled, sits in the center, providing a gentle contrast. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple fork and spoon beside it. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting, homely appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
A simple green salad on the side
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes, broth, and water. Bring to a simmer.
Add quartered artichoke hearts. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8-10 minutes.
Season soup with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls.
Place a spoonful of cottage cheese in the center of each bowl. Swirl lightly with a spoon.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Beef Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: The Beer-Braised Beef Noodle Soup is presented in a deep, dark ceramic bowl, showcasing a rich, dark amber broth with a slight sheen. Irregular, tender chunks of braised beef, approximately 3-4 cm cubes, are nestled amongst al dente wide wheat noodles, which are partially submerged in the aromatic liquid. Scattered throughout the broth are small, softened dice of red tomatoes, adding subtle color. A perfectly soft-boiled egg, halved lengthwise to reveal its creamy, slightly runny yolk, sits prominently on top. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped scallions provides a fresh contrast. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a pair of elegant chopsticks and a small white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and inviting textures, with appropriate negative space to emphasize the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in deep individual ceramic bowls
Provide chopsticks for eating noodles and beef
Offer a small spoon for broth
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, sliced ginger, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the beer. Scrape bottom of pot to release any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, star anise, cinnamon stick, dried chilies (if using), and beef stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
While beef braises, soft-boil eggs. Place eggs in boiling water for 6-7 minutes. Transfer to ice bath. Peel and halve lengthwise.
Cook wide wheat noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.

Divide cooked noodles among four deep individual serving bowls. Ladle generous portions of braised beef and broth over noodles. Top each bowl with two halved soft-boiled egg pieces. Garnish with chopped scallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lychee Glazed Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of two golden-brown chicken thighs, each cut into two or three thick, diagonal chunks, arranged slightly overlapping on one side of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous drizzle of the glossy, amber-hued lychee glaze coats the chicken, with some pooling at the base. Several whole, pearly-white lychee fruits are nestled alongside the chicken. A sprinkle of thinly sliced vibrant green onions and toasted sesame seeds garnishes the chicken and sauce. The dish showcases rich golden chicken, translucent amber glaze, bright white lychees, and vivid green onions. The plating maintains moderate negative space, with elements well-proportioned. The entire plate is shown in a modern bistro setting, with natural even lighting, featuring a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and a separate rice bowl for accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a portion of fluffy white jasmine rice in a small, separate rice bowl.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
In the same pan, reduce heat to medium. Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, and honey to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch and water to make a slurry. Stir slurry into simmering sauce. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Add lychees to the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Turn to coat chicken evenly with the glaze.
Drizzle with sesame oil.
Remove from heat.
notes: Adjust honey to taste for desired sweetness.
For spicier glaze, add a pinch of chili flakes with ginger and garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Carrot Root Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, sustainable salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The roasted beetroots, cut into 2 cm cubes, display deep ruby reds and caramelized edges, scattered among the bright orange carrot rounds and batons. Thinly sliced, pale pink quick-pickled red onion rings are interspersed throughout, offering a delicate contrast. Toasted walnut halves provide a rustic, crunchy texture. A light drizzle of the beet kvass dressing glistens on the vegetables, integrating all components. Fresh green parsley leaves are subtly sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh accent. The composition is natural and unforced, with appropriate negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural elements like green foliage, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash beetroots and carrots. Trim ends. Peel if desired.
Cut beetroots into 2 cm cubes. Cut carrots into 1 cm thick rounds or batons.
Toss beetroots and carrots with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Thinly slice red onion into rings.
Combine 120 ml water, 60 ml apple cider vinegar, 5 g sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Stir until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat.
Pour hot pickling liquid over red onion rings. Let steep for at least 15 minutes, or until cooled. Drain before use.
In a small bowl, whisk together 30 ml olive oil, beet kvass, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine roasted beetroots, carrots, drained pickled red onion, and toasted walnuts.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Potato and Egg Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, golden-brown Spanish tortilla rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. It is cut into thick wedges, revealing layers of tender, pale yellow potato slices and creamy, set egg. The potato pieces are soft and slightly translucent, interspersed with hints of caramelized onion. The exterior of the tortilla is a warm, inviting golden-brown, with a slightly irregular, homemade texture. Adjacent to the tortilla wedges are a few bright red, plump slices of fresh tomato, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is placed on a well-worn wooden dining table, with visible grain and minor imperfections. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. A simple, folded linen napkin and perhaps a fork are casually placed nearby. The overall presentation is homely, unpretentious, and comforting, inviting immediate enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of crusty bread.
Often enjoyed as a tapa or a simple meal.
Can be eaten warm or at room temperature.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a 20 cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Add thinly sliced potatoes and onion to the pan. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in oil.
Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are very tender but not browned. Stir occasionally.
Drain potatoes and onion through a colander. Reserve about 2 tablespoons of the drained oil in the pan. Let excess oil drain from potatoes for a few minutes.
Crack eggs into a large bowl. Whisk well with a fork. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Add drained potatoes and onion to the beaten eggs. Mix gently to coat all potatoes. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Heat the reserved olive oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Pour the egg and potato mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until the edges are set and golden. The center should still be a bit soft.
Place a large plate over the pan. Invert the pan to flip the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until set to your liking.
Slide the cooked tortilla onto a serving plate. Let rest for a few minutes before slicing.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sliced fresh tomatoes on the side.
notes: This recipe yields a classic "pincho de tortilla."
Adjust cooking time for desired doneness; some prefer a firmer tortilla, others a creamier, softer center.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thigh, Saffron Risotto, Crispy Sage
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white, modern designer plate holds a single, sophisticated serving. On the left, a pool of vibrant saffron risotto, its creamy, fluid texture evident, spreads organically across the porcelain. Its color is a rich, warm yellow, speckled with tiny orange saffron threads. To the right, a perfectly pan-seared boneless chicken thigh rests, its skin a deep, glossy golden-brown, taut and crispy, contrasting with the tender, juicy meat visible at the edges. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. A few delicate, emerald-green crispy sage leaves are strategically placed atop the chicken and around the risotto, providing a textural counterpoint and a fresh aromatic note. The plating emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the precise execution of each component. The scene is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and elegant simplicity. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the absolute focal point.
instructions: Heat chicken broth in a saucepan. Add saffron threads. Keep warm over low heat.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Do not brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add one ladle of hot saffron broth to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.

When rice is al dente, remove from heat. Stir in remaining 45 g cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until creamy and fluid. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season skin and flesh generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy.

Flip chicken thighs. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
While chicken rests, heat a small amount of olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry sage leaves for 30-60 seconds until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt.

Spoon a generous, fluid portion of saffron risotto onto the center-left of each plate, allowing it to spread organically. Place one rested chicken thigh, skin-side up, on the right side of the risotto, slightly overlapping. Garnish with a few crispy sage leaves placed artfully on top of the chicken and around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, tender from braising, are nestled together. A rich, glossy, dark brown mushroom sauce generously coats the chicken and pools elegantly on the plate. Sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the sauce. The dish is garnished with a small cluster of fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves and a delicate sprig of fresh thyme, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken maintains its whole, natural shape, not sliced. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, restaurant-style background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and softened.
Add diced shallots and minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Cook for 1 minute until reduced slightly.
Gradually whisk in beef stock until smooth. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Discard thyme sprigs.
Increase heat to medium-high. Simmer sauce for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened to desired consistency.
Stir in butter until melted and incorporated. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken with mushroom sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun-Spiced Plant-Based Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cajun-Spiced Plant-Based Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish forms a slightly mounded, inviting heap in the center of the plate, leaving moderate negative space around the edges. The long-grain rice is fluffy and tender, infused with a rich reddish-orange hue from the tomatoes, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper. Interspersed throughout the rice are tender, diced pieces of green, red, and yellow bell peppers, along with diced onion and celery. Nestled naturally on top and around the rice are several seared, golden-brown 2-3 cm chunks of plant-based chicken, showcasing a subtly firm exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley contrasts beautifully with the warm tones of the dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting for a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of hot sauce for extra spice.
Accompany with cornbread or crusty bread for soaking up juices.
instructions: Cut plant-based chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt, black pepper, and half of the cayenne pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear plant-based chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and celery to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally. This is the 'Holy Trinity'.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, dried thyme, dried oregano, and remaining cayenne pepper. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Pour in vegetable broth and diced tomatoes with their liquid. Bring to a boil, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared plant-based chicken to the pan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper to your preferred spice level.
Ensure plant-based chicken is thoroughly heated through.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Shin with Tomato and Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef shin is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, dark brown beef chunks are fork-tender, nestled in a glossy, deep red tomato and vegetable sauce. The sauce is thick, clinging to the beef, with visible pieces of finely diced carrot, celery, and onion. A vibrant green gremolata, a mix of finely chopped fresh parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic, is sprinkled generously over the beef and sauce, adding a bright color contrast and fresh aroma. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish. The setting includes a simple wooden table surface, traditional Italian flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a softly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy polenta or saffron risotto to absorb the rich sauce.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping.
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar complements the richness.

ingredients.name: Beef shin, bone-in, cut into 4 cm thick rounds

instructions: Pat beef shin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef shin rounds until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared beef shin to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in the liquid. If not, add more stock or water.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Turn beef occasionally during cooking.
Remove beef from the pot. Discard rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Skim excess fat from the sauce.
To make Gremolata: Combine finely chopped parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed. If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered to reduce.
Serve braised beef shin with the rich tomato sauce. Garnish generously with Gremolata.
notes: Braising time may vary depending on the beef cut and desired tenderness. Ensure meat is fall-apart tender.
This dish benefits from being made a day ahead, allowing flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Mushroom and Broccoli Risotto rests in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, positioned on a natural wooden table. The risotto is fluid and spreads gently, showcasing its characteristic "all'onda" consistency. Earthy brown sautéed mushrooms are interspersed throughout, along with small, vibrant green broccoli florets that retain a tender-crisp texture. A generous sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley adds a contrasting green hue. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the surface. The dish is presented with a silver fork beside the bowl and a simple, folded white linen napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting the glossy texture of the risotto and the rich colors of the vegetables against the minimalist backdrop. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, embodying casual Italian dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, often as a primo piatto (first course) in a multi-course Italian meal, or as a main course.
Pair with a crisp white wine.
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it hot over low heat.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in minced garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add one ladleful of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is almost completely absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Allow each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Five minutes before risotto is done, add small broccoli florets to the pan. They should cook to tender-crisp.
Risotto should be creamy. Rice grains should be al dente, firm to the bite but not hard.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold diced butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until butter and cheese are fully incorporated. Risotto should be creamy and glossy.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Curry with Eggplant (Murgh Aloo Baingan)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich Chicken and Potato Curry with Eggplant is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The curry, a deep reddish-brown, features tender, slow-cooked chicken chunks, soft 2cm potato cubes, and creamy 2cm eggplant cubes, all bathed in a thick, aromatic gravy. Fluffy basmati rice is neatly piled beside the curry. Freshly chopped cilantro leaves are scattered over the curry, with a few thin green chili slices for a vibrant color and mild heat. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, alongside a folded white cotton napkin and a polished stainless steel fork. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm tones of the authentic Indian meal. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti.
Often accompanied by raita (yogurt dip) or pickled vegetables.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Dice potatoes and eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Finely chop onion, garlic, and ginger. Slice green chilies.
Rinse basmati rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, and red chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to temper spices.
Add chopped tomatoes and green chilies. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and oil separates.
Add chicken chunks, potato cubes, and eggplant cubes to the pot. Stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water or chicken broth. Add salt to taste. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F), potatoes are tender, and eggplant is soft. Stir occasionally.
Stir in garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Stir in fresh chopped cilantro just before serving.
Serve hot with basmati rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, crispy chicken cutlet, topped with melted fresh mozzarella, is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a neatly coiled nest of al dente spaghetti, glistening with vibrant red tomato pomodoro sauce. A few fresh, emerald-green basil leaves are artfully scattered over both the chicken and pasta. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The dish sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. A single set of silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting ambiance typical of a modern bistro, with a clean background. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread, such as ciabatta or focaccia, for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a simple side salad with a vinaigrette dressing.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50 g, grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs mixed with 20g grated Parmesan.
Dredge each chicken piece in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to coat well.

Heat 100 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken cutlets 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Drain on paper towels.
While chicken cooks, prepare tomato sauce. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Place a slice or two of fresh mozzarella on each hot chicken cutlet. Return to warm skillet or baking dish to melt cheese, or briefly broil.
Toss cooked spaghetti with half of the tomato sauce. Reserve remaining sauce for serving.
To plate, arrange a portion of sauced spaghetti on a plate. Place one mozzarella-topped chicken cutlet beside the pasta.
Spoon a little extra tomato sauce over the chicken and pasta. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately with extra grated Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For extra crispiness, lightly toast the breadcrumbs before coating the chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Rice Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two vibrant, roasted bell pepper halves on a clean white porcelain plate, each generously filled. The red and yellow peppers are tender with slightly charred edges, holding their shape. Inside, the savory beef and rice stuffing is mounded high, revealing browned ground beef, soft white rice, and bright green parsley. A golden-brown crust of melted Parmesan cheese crowns the stuffing. Around the base, a rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce pools gently, its glossy surface speckled with thyme. The sauce adds color and moisture. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Peppers are cut lengthwise, presenting a substantial portion. The scene features a simple light wooden table, a clean white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, highlighting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in the tomato sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef to skillet. Brown beef, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cooked rice, half of the chopped fresh thyme, half of the chopped parsley, 25g grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, remaining thyme, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spoon beef and rice mixture evenly into bell pepper halves.
Pour tomato sauce around stuffed peppers in the baking dish.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil. Sprinkle remaining 25g Parmesan cheese over stuffed peppers.
Bake uncovered for another 20-25 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is golden.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality ground beef (e.g., 80/20 lean-to-fat ratio).
Par-cooking the rice before mixing ensures even cooking and a tender texture in the final dish.
Adjust seasoning to taste, especially salt and pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken and Fermented Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken and Fermented Garlic Pasta is presented on a round, matte, off-white ceramic plate, allowing ample negative space. A loose mound of al dente rigatoni forms the base. Thick, irregular golden-brown chicken chunks are naturally nestled amongst the pasta. Deep green, wilted kale leaves and dark purple Kalamata olives are scattered throughout, adding color and texture. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens, and fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final, natural garnish. The dish sits on a light reclaimed wood table. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean and minimalistic, with a blurred green plant suggesting natural elements.

ingredients.name: Fresh kale, stems removed, roughly chopped

instructions: Prepare quick fermented garlic paste: Blend peeled garlic cloves with 5g salt and 30ml water until a coarse paste forms. Transfer to a clean jar. Loosely cover. Let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours to begin fermentation. Refrigerate for later use.
Cut chicken thighs into thick, irregular chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions in a large pot of salted water until al dente. Reserve 125ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
In the same skillet, add another 15ml olive oil. Add 30g of the quick fermented garlic paste and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped kale to the skillet. Sauté until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Add pitted Kalamata olives and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.

Add cooked rigatoni and cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Toss to combine. If needed, add reserved pasta water gradually to achieve desired sauce consistency. Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and a drizzle of remaining 30ml olive oil.
notes: Utilize vegetable scraps (e.g., onion skins, carrot peels, herb stems) to make homemade vegetable stock, minimizing food waste.
The quick fermented garlic paste provides a deeper, more complex flavor profile while utilizing a preservation technique.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Chocolate-Lemon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a tender, juicy interior with a golden-brown crust, sits centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is either presented whole or in two to three thick, unsliced chunks. A rich, glossy, dark brown spicy chocolate-lemon sauce is artfully spooned over and around the chicken, pooling gently on the plate. Alongside, a neat arrangement of golden-brown, halved baby potatoes and vibrant green asparagus spears adds color and texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley and yellow lemon zest garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss halved baby potatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.

Add trimmed asparagus spears to the baking sheet with potatoes. Toss lightly with remaining olive oil. Continue roasting for another 10-15 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and asparagus is crisp-tender.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Add chopped dark chocolate and hot sauce. Stir until chocolate is melted and sauce is smooth. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in fresh lemon juice and butter until butter is melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick chunks or serve whole. Plate chicken with roasted potatoes and asparagus. Spoon generous amounts of spicy chocolate-lemon sauce over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon zest.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken with Caramelized Onion Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, crisply seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and whole, is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beneath and around the chicken are rich, deeply caramelized onion slices, thinly cut into crescent shapes, forming a tender bed. A glossy, dark amber jus is spooned generously over the chicken and onions, reflecting the light. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish, adding a vibrant green accent. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table surface, with a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the chicken's crispy skin and the jus's deep hue, creating a refined bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Pommes de Terre Gratin (potatoes au gratin)
Serve with simple steamed haricots verts (green beans)
Accompany with crusty baguette for soaking up the jus
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.

Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the same pan. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and tender. Do not rush this step.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs to the pan with the onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Reduce wine by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring the liquid to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid.
Transfer the pan to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pan. Place on a plate and tent loosely with foil to keep warm.
Place the pan back on the stovetop over medium-high heat. Reduce the sauce until it slightly thickens to a jus consistency. This takes 5-10 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken with caramelized onions and a generous spooning of the jus.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Caramelizing onions properly takes time and patience; do not rush this step for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cod with Spiced Fennel and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown baked cod rests in a shallow white ceramic bowl. The cod, presented as a thick, whole fillet, is nestled within a vibrant red-orange sauce. The sauce, rich and slightly chunky, features tender, pale green fennel wedges and flecks of minced garlic. A few thin slices of bright yellow lemon are placed beside the cod. The dish is generously sprinkled with vivid green chopped fresh coriander, adding a pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. A rustic, crusty bread roll is subtly visible in the soft background, hinting at a complete Mediterranean dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a side of fluffy couscous or rice.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half juiced, half sliced for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add fennel wedges. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, black pepper, and crushed fennel seeds. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Season the sauce with salt to taste.
Nestle cod fillets into the simmering sauce. Ensure cod is partially submerged.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until cod is opaque and flakes easily.
Remove from oven. Discard bay leaf.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the baked cod.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander. Serve immediately.
notes: For deeper flavor, toast whole cumin and coriander seeds before grinding.
Adjust spice levels to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Vegetarian Sausage Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Fermented Tomato & Vegetarian Sausage Rice Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl. Fluffy brown rice forms the base. Artfully arranged on top are golden-brown, roasted potato cubes, approximately 2cm, skins left on. Thick, seared vegetarian sausage chunks, about 2cm, display a rich, savory crust. Bright green peas are scattered. A generous dollop of vivid red, finely diced fermented tomato and chili relish crowns the dish, its freshness contrasting with cooked elements. A few sprigs of fresh parsley provide a subtle, natural garnish. The composition is clean and organic, with ample negative space. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish against a minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato-Chili Relish: Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Finely mince chili. Combine tomatoes, chili, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix well. Let sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour, or ideally 4-6 hours, stirring occasionally.
Cook Rice: Rinse brown rice. Cook according to package directions until water is absorbed and rice is tender.

Roast Potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes or wedges, keeping skins on. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and lightly browned.

Cook Sausage and Vegetables: Slice vegetarian sausages into 2cm thick rounds or chunks. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage pieces. Cook until browned on all sides. Remove from pan.

Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Return sausage to the pan. Add green peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes, until peas are tender. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble: Divide cooked rice among 4 bowls. Arrange roasted potato cubes and sausage-pea mixture over the rice. Spoon generous amount of fermented tomato-chili relish over each serving. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.
notes: For deeper flavor, prepare the fermented tomato-chili relish 12-24 hours in advance. Store at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Shrimp and Fennel Linguine with Capers
recipes.visual_description: A modest individual portion of Shrimp and Fennel Linguine with Capers is served on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a rustic edge. The linguine is loosely coiled in the center, glistening with a creamy, pale sauce. Pan-seared pink shrimp, with tails on, are nestled among the pasta strands. Thinly sliced, tender fennel pieces are distributed throughout the dish, adding light green and pale yellow tones. Coarsely chopped fresh parsley is scattered generously over the top, providing vibrant green flecks. The dish is presented on a well-used light wooden dining table, with a standard fork and knife casually placed beside the plate on a rumpled linen napkin. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting colors. The background shows blurred elements of a lived-in kitchen, suggesting a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping

ingredients.name: Large shrimp, peeled, deveined, tails on

instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Trim and thinly slice fennel bulbs. Mince garlic and shallot.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced fennel to the skillet. Cook 8-10 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Add minced shallot and garlic. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.
Pour white wine into the hot skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Stir in vegetable broth, heavy cream, and drained capers. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 3 minutes to slightly thicken.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Return cooked shrimp to the skillet. Add fresh lemon juice and chopped parsley.
Toss everything together. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure shrimp is not overcooked to maintain tenderness and succulence.
Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Argentinian Beef Skewers with Chimichurri and Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Argentinian Beef Skewers is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. Three beef skewers, each holding three to four 3cm seared beef cubes, are arranged slightly fanned, showcasing their rich brown crust and tender interior. Beside the skewers, a pile of golden-brown, crispy 2cm potato wedges are neatly stacked. A vibrant green chimichurri sauce is generously drizzled over the beef and potatoes, with a small pool beside them for dipping. A fresh sprig of parsley garnishes the dish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A folded cotton napkin and a simple glass are placed beside the plate, completing a modern bistro setting with an authentic Argentinian touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in extra chimichurri.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm wedges. Place potatoes in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes. Drain potatoes thoroughly.
Toss par-boiled potatoes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crispy.
While potatoes roast, prepare chimichurri. Finely chop parsley, oregano, and garlic. Combine chopped herbs and garlic in a bowl.
Add red wine vinegar, 100 ml olive oil, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper to herb mixture. Stir well to combine. Set aside.
Cut beef into 3cm cubes. Thread beef cubes onto skewers. Season beef skewers generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large grill pan or outdoor grill to high. Lightly oil the grates or pan. Sear beef skewers for 4-5 minutes per side until a rich brown crust forms and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove beef skewers from heat. Let them rest for 5 minutes.
Arrange beef skewers and crispy potatoes on plates. Drizzle generously with chimichurri sauce. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes in chimichurri to your spice preference.
Ensure potatoes are thoroughly drained before roasting for maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Trinidadian Mincemeat Pelau
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Trinidadian Mincemeat Pelau is centered on a rustic, round ceramic plate. The rice is a rich, warm brown from the caramelized sugar, interspersed with darker chunks of seared mincemeat and creamy, light brown pigeon peas. Individual grains of long-grain rice are distinct, fluffy, and tender. A few fresh green thyme leaves are scattered over the top. A small wedge of bright green lime sits casually on the rim of the plate. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and natural wear. In the background, slightly out of focus, is a small, clear glass bowl holding a simple side salad of thinly sliced red tomato and crisp green cucumber. A small, traditional West Indian hot pepper sauce bottle or a small ceramic dish of homemade pepper sauce is placed nearby. A casually folded, plain cloth napkin and a simple fork rest beside the plate. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a simple side salad (e.g., sliced cucumber, tomato, or coleslaw).
Accompanied by pepper sauce (hot sauce).
Often enjoyed as a hearty one-pot meal for family gatherings.

ingredients.name: Pimento peppers, finely chopped (or 1/2 small bell pepper, diced)

instructions: Season mincemeat with 2 tablespoons green seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add brown sugar. Cook until sugar melts and turns dark amber, stirring constantly. This is the "browning" step.
Add seasoned mincemeat to the pot. Break up with a spoon. Brown mincemeat, stirring occasionally, until no pink remains. Cook for 8-10 minutes.
Stir in diced onion, minced garlic, chopped pimento peppers, and remaining 1 tablespoon green seasoning. Cook for 3-5 minutes until aromatics soften.
Add rice and drained pigeon peas. Stir well to coat. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and water or broth. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let pelau rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Remove thyme sprigs. Serve hot.
notes: Green seasoning is a crucial aromatic blend for authentic Caribbean flavor. It can be prepared by blending fresh herbs like thyme, chives, parsley, culantro (bandhaniya), garlic, onion, and pimento peppers with a splash of vinegar or lime juice.
The 'browning' step, caramelizing sugar in oil, is essential for Pelau's characteristic color and deep, savory-sweet flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Gambas con Patatas y Cebolla Caramelizada
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A mound of golden-brown potato cubes forms the base, each piece with a slight crisp exterior and soft interior. Nestle among the potatoes are succulent, rosy-pink shrimp, perfectly cooked and retaining their natural curl, with tails intact. Interspersed throughout are strands of deeply caramelized onions, their rich, amber hue contrasting with the lighter tones of the potatoes and shrimp. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color and freshness over the entire composition. A vibrant yellow lemon wedge sits neatly beside the main mound. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The background features a simple wooden table surface and a casually folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
Pair with a glass of dry Fino sherry or a light Spanish white wine.
instructions: Slice onions thinly. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally. Remove from pan.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until tender but still firm, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add drained potato cubes. Cook until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Push potatoes to one side of the pan. Add minced garlic to the empty side. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the pan with potatoes and garlic. Sprinkle with smoked paprika. Cook shrimp for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcook.
Pour in dry sherry. Cook for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return caramelized onions to the pan. Add saffron and its steeping liquid. Stir gently to combine all ingredients. Cook for 1-2 minutes until heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
